tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

input.plan:
# Plan — Ridgeline RFQ Inbox parser (structure + build order)

## Context
Build `parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json` per `data/README.md`: classify each .eml (7 kinds),
extract self-contained line items, flag needs_review. Must be replayable with no key (committed
cache), idempotent (2nd run = 0 calls), crash-proof per email, and cost-reported. Graded on a
held-out ~40-email inbox, so no dev-specific logic. CLAUDE.md already fixes the architecture; this
plan lays out files and order. One model call per email (OpenAI structured output, vision for
scans/photos); code owns threads/dupes/validation.

Housekeeping noticed: repo has `gitignore` (no dot) — rename to `.gitignore`, and add a rule so
`cache/` is **committed** (needed for replay). `.git` looks partially initialised; verify with
`git status` before first commit.

## Folder structure
```
pyproject.toml            # console script `parse` -> rfq.cli:main; deps pinned
requirements.txt          # openai, pydantic, openpyxl, pdfplumber, pypdfium2, Pillow, python-docx, beautifulsoup4, pytest
RUNNING.md  DECISIONS.md  AI_USAGE.md  MATCHER.md (optional)
parsed.json               # dev output, regenerated
rfq/
  cli.py                  # argparse: parse --emails --out [--retry-failed RUN] [--no-llm]
  config.py               # model name, prompt_version, prices, page/image caps, timeouts
  models.py               # Doc, Line(row_id,text,struck,...), Attachment, Email dataclasses
  mime.py                 # headers, body text/html->text, quoted-history split, forwards, cid images, nested .eml
  extractors/
    __init__.py           # dispatch by mime/extension; wraps each in try/except -> Doc(error=...)
    xlsx.py csv_.py docx.py pdf.py image.py html.py
  dedupe.py               # duplicate_of: normalised content hash, later Date: is dup
  threads.py              # revises: In-Reply-To/References/subject chain -> inbox id
  prompt.py               # system prompt + render Email/Docs with row IDs  ([body!B12], [Sheet!R5], [f.pdf!P1L8])
  schema.py               # Pydantic discriminated union: RFQ | Revision | PurchaseOrder | NoItems
  llm.py                  # OpenAI client, retries (429/5xx/timeout), one repair retry, vision parts
  cache.py                # cache/<sha256>.json; key = model+prompt_version+rendered input (+image hashes)
  validate.py             # row_id grounding, refill raw/qty/uom from source, drop struck/unknown rows,
                          # qty≠size/sch/class/price, uom normalise, silent-loss guard, needs_review only for request kinds
  pipeline.py             # per-email: mime -> extract -> render -> cache/llm -> validate -> merge dedupe/threads
  costlog.py              # runs/<id>/calls.jsonl, failures.jsonl (retryable flag), reports/cost.md
  matcher.py              # optional, code-only attribute match
cache/                    # committed model responses
runs/latest/              # committed last run logs
reports/  eval.md cost.md
eval/eval.py              # scores vs answer_key.json (only place that reads it); per-component modes
tests/                    # unit tests per extractor/validator + synthetic fixtures (not dev strings)
app/                      # optional FastAPI + one HTML page, read-only
ai-sessions/              # exported logs at the end
```

## Build order (each step: pytest -q, run parse on dev, eval when available, stop & report)
1. **Skeleton + contract** — pyproject, `cli.py`, `config.py`, `models.py`; `parse` writes a stub
   entry per email (`other`, needs_review=false) and passes `check_format.py`. Per-email try/except
   from day one.
2. **Eval harness early** — `eval/eval.py` implementing the README metrics (silent losses,
   hallucinated lines, lost/phantom, class acc, line P/R with pairing on `raw` tokens, qty/uom/source,
   must_mention/must_not_mention with spelling equivalences, links, review P/R) → `reports/eval.md`.
   Gives a baseline number before any model work.
3. **MIME layer** — `mime.py` (reuse logic from `data/eml_to_json.py`), quoted-history split,
   forwards from @ridgeline-supply.example, nested .eml, inline cid images. Dump an inspection
   view of all 24 emails to study them (scratch only).
4. **Extractors** — xlsx (hidden sheets, merged cells, strikethrough, sheet names), csv, docx
   (body order), pdf (encrypted→error, text vs scanned→page images, page cap), image (tiny-logo
   filter), html. Each returns a `Doc`, never raises; tests with small synthetic files incl. broken ones.
5. **Code-only signals** — `dedupe.py`, `threads.py`; check links against eval.
6. **Model call** — `schema.py`, `prompt.py`, `cache.py`, `llm.py`, `costlog.py`. No-key/cache-miss
   → flagged entry. Run once on dev with key, commit cache; re-run without key to prove replay + 0 calls.
7. **Validation** — `validate.py` grounding/refill/guards; iterate prompt vs eval, inspecting
   changed lines before fixing (general causes only).
8. **Robustness** — failures.jsonl + `--retry-failed`, timeouts, oversize inputs; final cost report.
9. **Docs** — RUNNING.md, DECISIONS.md (4 required sections + time spent), AI_USAGE.md.
10. **Optional, if time** — matcher.py + MATCHER.md, then app/.

## Verification
- `python data/check_format.py parsed.json --emails data/dev/emails` → exit 0.
- `python eval/eval.py parsed.json` → reports/eval.md numbers.
- Unset OPENAI_API_KEY, rerun parse → identical parsed.json, `calls.jsonl` shows 0 live calls.
- Corrupt-attachment test fixture → that email flagged, run completes.

# Plan — Ridgeline RFQ Inbox parser (structure + build order)

## Context
Build `parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json` per `data/README.md`: classify each .eml (7 kinds),
extract self-contained line items, flag needs_review. Must be replayable with no key (committed
cache), idempotent (2nd run = 0 calls), crash-proof per email, and cost-reported. Graded on a
held-out ~40-email inbox, so no dev-specific logic. CLAUDE.md already fixes the architecture; this
plan lays out files and order. One model call per email (OpenAI structured output, vision for
scans/photos); code owns threads/dupes/validation.

Housekeeping noticed: repo has `gitignore` (no dot) — rename to `.gitignore`, and add a rule so
`cache/` is **committed** (needed for replay). `.git` looks partially initialised; verify with
`git status` before first commit.

## Folder structure
```

requirements.txt          # openai, pydantic, openpyxl, pdfplumber, pypdfium2, Pillow, python-docx, beautifulsoup4, pytest
RUNNING.md  DECISIONS.md  AI_USAGE.md  MATCHER.md (optional)
parsed.json               # dev output, regenerated
rfq/
  cli.py                  # argparse: parse --emails --out [--retry-failed RUN] [--no-llm]
  config.py               # model name, prompt_version, prices, page/image caps, timeouts
  models.py               # Doc, Line(row_id,text,struck,...), Attachment, Email dataclasses
  mime.py                 # headers, body text/html->text, quoted-history split, forwards, cid images, nested .eml
  extractors/
    __init__.py           # dispatch by mime/extension; wraps each in try/except -> Doc(error=...)
    xlsx.py csv_.py docx.py pdf.py image.py html.py
  dedupe.py               # duplicate_of: normalised content hash, later Date: is dup
  threads.py              # revises: In-Reply-To/References/subject chain -> inbox id
  prompt.py               # system prompt + render Email/Docs with row IDs  ([body!B12], [Sheet!R5], [f.pdf!P1L8])
  schema.py               # Pydantic discriminated union: RFQ | Revision | PurchaseOrder | NoItems
  llm.py                  # OpenAI client, retries (429/5xx/timeout), one repair retry, vision parts
  cache.py                # cache/<sha256>.json; key = model+prompt_version+rendered input (+image hashes)
  validate.py             # row_id grounding, refill raw/qty/uom from source, drop struck/unknown rows,
                          # qty≠size/sch/class/price, uom normalise, silent-loss guard, needs_review only for request kinds
  pipeline.py             # per-email: mime -> extract -> render -> cache/llm -> validate -> merge dedupe/threads
  costlog.py              # runs/<id>/calls.jsonl, failures.jsonl (retryable flag), reports/cost.md
  matcher.py              # optional, code-only attribute match
cache/                    # committed model responses
runs/latest/              # committed last run logs
reports/  eval.md cost.md
eval/eval.py              # scores vs answer_key.json (only place that reads it); per-component modes
tests/                    # unit tests per extractor/validator + synthetic fixtures (not dev strings)
app/                      # optional FastAPI + one HTML page, read-only
ai-sessions/              # exported logs at the end
```

1. **Skeleton + contract** — pyproject, `cli.py`, `config.py`, `models.py`; `parse` writes a stub
   entry per email (`other`, needs_review=false) and passes `check_format.py`. Per-email try/except
   from day one.
2. **Eval harness early** — `eval/eval.py` implementing the README metrics (silent losses,
   hallucinated lines, lost/phantom, class acc, line P/R with pairing on `raw` tokens, qty/uom/source,
   must_mention/must_not_mention with spelling equivalences, links, review P/R) → `reports/eval.md`.
   Gives a baseline number before any model work.
3. **MIME layer** — `mime.py` (reuse logic from `data/eml_to_json.py`), quoted-history split,
   forwards from @ridgeline-supply.example, nested .eml, inline cid images. Dump an inspection
   view of all 24 emails to study them (scratch only).
4. **Extractors** — xlsx (hidden sheets, merged cells, strikethrough, sheet names), csv, docx

   filter), html. Each returns a `Doc`, never raises; tests with small synthetic files incl. broken ones.

   → flagged entry. Run once on dev with key, commit cache; re-run without key to prove replay + 0 calls.

   changed lines before fixing (general causes only).
8. **Robustness** — failures.jsonl + `--retry-failed`, timeouts, oversize inputs; final cost report.
9. **Docs** — RUNNING.md, DECISIONS.md (4 required sections + time spent), AI_USAGE.md.
10. **Optional, if time** — matcher.py + MATCHER.md, then app/.

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path

try:  # .env is optional; a missing python-dotenv must not break the run
    from dotenv import load_dotenv

    load_dotenv(override=False)
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
    pass

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CACHE_DIR = ROOT / "cache"
RUNS_DIR = ROOT / "runs"
REPORTS_DIR = ROOT / "reports"

MODEL = os.environ.get("RFQ_MODEL", "gpt-4.1-mini")
PROMPT_VERSION = "v0"
TEMPERATURE = 0.0
REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S = 90
MAX_RETRIES = 3

# Input caps (protect cost and latency on pathological attachments)
MAX_PDF_PAGES = 20
MAX_IMAGES_PER_EMAIL = 12
MIN_IMAGE_SIDE_PX = 64  # smaller inline images are treated as logos / signatures

VALID_UOMS = ("EA", "FT", "M", "IN", "BX", "PK", "PR", "DZ", "RL", "LB", "SET", "GAL", "BAG", "CS")
CLASSIFICATIONS = (
    "rfq",
    "rfq_revision",
    "purchase_order",
    "vendor_quote",
    "status_inquiry",
    "auto_reply",
    "other",
)
REQUEST_KINDS = ("rfq", "rfq_revision", "purchase_order")
OUR_DOMAIN = "ridgeline-supply.example"


def api_key_present() -> bool:
    """True if a key is configured. Never returns or prints the key itself."""
    return bool(os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", "").strip())

"""Plain data types shared across the pipeline."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Any


@dataclass
class Line:
    """One addressable line of text extracted from the email or an attachment."""

    row_id: str  # stable id shown to the model, e.g. "body!B12", "Sheet1!R5", "a.pdf!P1L8"
    text: str
    struck: bool = False  # strikethrough / crossed out in the source
    cells: list[str] | None = None  # table cells, when the line is a table row


@dataclass
class Doc:
    """What an extractor produced from one source. Extractors never raise; they set `error`."""

    source: str  # "body" or the attachment filename
    kind: str  # body | xlsx | csv | docx | pdf | image | html | eml | unknown
    lines: list[Line] = field(default_factory=list)
    images: list[bytes] = field(default_factory=list)  # PNG bytes for vision (scans, photos)
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # context: sheet names, hidden sheets skipped, ...
    error: str | None = None  # set when the source could not be read


@dataclass
class Attachment:
    filename: str
    mime: str
    data: bytes
    inline: bool = False
    content_id: str | None = None


@dataclass
class Email:
    id: str
    headers: dict[str, str | None]
    body: str  # current message text, quoted history removed
    quoted: str = ""  # quoted history (context only, never a line source)
    attachments: list[Attachment] = field(default_factory=list)


@dataclass
class LineItem:
    raw: str
    description: str
    qty: float | None
    uom: str | None
    source: str


@dataclass
class Result:
    classification: str
    revises: str | None = None
    duplicate_of: str | None = None
    needs_review: bool = False
    review_reason: str | None = None
    line_items: list[LineItem] = field(default_factory=list)

    def to_json(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

"""Per-email processing. Step 1: stub only — every email becomes `other`.

Later steps replace `process_email` with mime -> extract -> prompt -> cache/llm -> validate.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.models import Result

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def process_email(path: Path) -> Result:
    """Stub: reads the file (so unreadable files fail here) and returns an empty `other`."""
    path.read_bytes()
    return Result(classification="other")


def failed_result(reason: str) -> Result:
    """Entry for an email we could not process at all.

    We don't know what it is, so it is treated as a possible request and flagged: a human
    looking at a non-request costs minutes; a silently dropped request costs a customer.
    """
    return Result(classification="rfq", needs_review=True, review_reason=reason)


def process_inbox(emails_dir: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for path in sorted(emails_dir.glob("*.eml")):
        try:
            result = process_email(path)
        except Exception as e:  # one bad email never takes down the run
            log.exception("failed on %s", path.name)
            result = failed_result(f"could not process email: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        out[path.stem] = result.to_json()
    return out

"""Command line: `rfq parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json` (or `python -m rfq parse ...`)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.pipeline import process_inbox


def _write_json_atomic(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    tmp.replace(path)


def cmd_parse(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    emails_dir = Path(args.emails)
    if not emails_dir.is_dir():
        print(f"--emails: not a directory: {emails_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    results = process_inbox(emails_dir)
    _write_json_atomic(Path(args.out), results)
    print(f"wrote {len(results)} emails to {args.out}")
    return 0


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="rfq", description="Ridgeline RFQ inbox parser")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("parse", help="parse every .eml in a directory")
    p.add_argument("--emails", required=True, help="directory of .eml files")
    p.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output JSON path")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_parse)
    return ap


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
        sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    return args.func(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.cli import main
from rfq.pipeline import process_inbox

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def test_every_email_appears_and_shape_ok(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "A1.eml").write_bytes(b"Subject: hi\r\n\r\nhello\r\n")
    (tmp_path / "A2.eml").write_bytes(b"Subject: two\r\n\r\nbody\r\n")
    out = tmp_path / "parsed.json"
    assert main(["parse", "--emails", str(tmp_path), "--out", str(out)]) == 0
    data = json.loads(out.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert set(data) == {"A1", "A2"}
    check = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "data" / "check_format.py"), str(out), "--emails", str(tmp_path)],
        capture_output=True,
    )
    assert check.returncode == 0, check.stdout


def test_one_bad_email_does_not_crash(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "good.eml").write_bytes(b"Subject: ok\r\n\r\nx\r\n")
    (tmp_path / "bad.eml").write_bytes(b"Subject: boom\r\n\r\nx\r\n")

    import rfq.pipeline as pl

    real = pl.process_email

    def flaky(path: Path):
        if path.stem == "bad":
            raise ValueError("simulated")
        return real(path)

    monkeypatch.setattr(pl, "process_email", flaky)
    data = process_inbox(tmp_path)
    assert data["good"]["classification"] == "other"
    assert data["bad"]["needs_review"] is True
    assert "simulated" in data["bad"]["review_reason"]

"""Plain data types shared across the pipeline."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Any


@dataclass
class Line:
    """One addressable line of text extracted from the email or an attachment."""

    row_id: str  # stable id shown to the model, e.g. "body!B12", "Sheet1!R5", "a.pdf!P1L8"
    text: str
    struck: bool = False  # strikethrough / crossed out in the source
    cells: list[str] | None = None  # table cells, when the line is a table row


@dataclass
class Doc:
    """What an extractor produced from one source. Extractors never raise; they set `error`."""

    source: str  # "body" or the attachment filename
    kind: str  # body | xlsx | csv | docx | pdf | image | html | eml | unknown
    lines: list[Line] = field(default_factory=list)
    images: list[bytes] = field(default_factory=list)  # PNG bytes for vision (scans, photos)
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # context: sheet names, hidden sheets skipped, ...
    error: str | None = None  # set when the source could not be read


@dataclass
class Attachment:
    filename: str
    mime: str
    data: bytes
    inline: bool = False
    content_id: str | None = None


@dataclass
class Email:
    id: str
    headers: dict[str, str | None]
    body: str  # current message text, quoted history removed
    quoted: str = ""  # quoted history (context only, never a line source)
    attachments: list[Attachment] = field(default_factory=list)


@dataclass
class LineItem:
    raw: str
    description: str
    qty: float | None
    uom: str | None
    source: str


@dataclass
class Result:
    classification: str
    revises: str | None = None
    duplicate_of: str | None = None
    needs_review: bool = False
    review_reason: str | None = None
    line_items: list[LineItem] = field(default_factory=list)

    def to_json(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

"""Per-email processing. Step 1: stub only — every email becomes `other`.

Later steps replace `process_email` with mime -> extract -> prompt -> cache/llm -> validate.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.models import Result

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def process_email(path: Path) -> Result:
    """Stub: reads the file (so unreadable files fail here) and returns an empty `other`."""
    path.read_bytes()
    return Result(classification="other")


def failed_result(reason: str) -> Result:
    """Entry for an email we could not process at all.

    We don't know what it is, so it is treated as a possible request and flagged: a human
    looking at a non-request costs minutes; a silently dropped request costs a customer.
    """
    return Result(classification="rfq", needs_review=True, review_reason=reason)


def process_inbox(emails_dir: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for path in sorted(emails_dir.glob("*.eml")):
        try:
            result = process_email(path)
        except Exception as e:  # one bad email never takes down the run
            log.exception("failed on %s", path.name)
            result = failed_result(f"could not process email: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        out[path.stem] = result.to_json()
    return out

"""Command line: `rfq parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json` (or `python -m rfq parse ...`)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.pipeline import process_inbox


def _write_json_atomic(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    tmp.replace(path)


def cmd_parse(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    emails_dir = Path(args.emails)
    if not emails_dir.is_dir():
        print(f"--emails: not a directory: {emails_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    results = process_inbox(emails_dir)
    _write_json_atomic(Path(args.out), results)
    print(f"wrote {len(results)} emails to {args.out}")
    return 0


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="rfq", description="Ridgeline RFQ inbox parser")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("parse", help="parse every .eml in a directory")
    p.add_argument("--emails", required=True, help="directory of .eml files")
    p.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output JSON path")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_parse)
    return ap


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
        sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    return args.func(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.cli import main
from rfq.pipeline import process_inbox

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def test_every_email_appears_and_shape_ok(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "A1.eml").write_bytes(b"Subject: hi\r\n\r\nhello\r\n")
    (tmp_path / "A2.eml").write_bytes(b"Subject: two\r\n\r\nbody\r\n")
    out = tmp_path / "parsed.json"
    assert main(["parse", "--emails", str(tmp_path), "--out", str(out)]) == 0
    data = json.loads(out.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert set(data) == {"A1", "A2"}
    check = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "data" / "check_format.py"), str(out), "--emails", str(tmp_path)],
        capture_output=True,
    )
    assert check.returncode == 0, check.stdout


def test_one_bad_email_does_not_crash(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "good.eml").write_bytes(b"Subject: ok\r\n\r\nx\r\n")
    (tmp_path / "bad.eml").write_bytes(b"Subject: boom\r\n\r\nx\r\n")

    import rfq.pipeline as pl

    real = pl.process_email

    def flaky(path: Path):
        if path.stem == "bad":
            raise ValueError("simulated")
        return real(path)

    monkeypatch.setattr(pl, "process_email", flaky)
    data = process_inbox(tmp_path)
    assert data["good"]["classification"] == "other"
    assert data["bad"]["needs_review"] is True
    assert "simulated" in data["bad"]["review_reason"]

- **[rfq/models.py](rfq/models.py)**: shared data types for the pipeline and the output.
- **[rfq/pipeline.py](rfq/pipeline.py)**: a placeholder that marks every email `other`. Each email is wrapped so that one failure can't stop the run.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Score parsed.json against the dev answer key, following data/README.md "What we grade".

    python eval/eval.py parsed.json
    python eval/eval.py parsed.json --detail lines          # per-line failures only
    python eval/eval.py parsed.json --emails E003,E007      # restrict to some emails
    python eval/eval.py parsed.json --baseline reports/eval.json   # what changed since last run

Writes reports/eval.md (human) and reports/eval.json (per-email/per-line outcomes, for diffs).
This is the ONLY code in the repo allowed to read answer_key.json.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from rapidfuzz import fuzz

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DEFAULT_KEY = ROOT / "data" / "dev" / "answer_key.json"
REQUEST_KINDS = {"rfq", "rfq_revision", "purchase_order"}
PAIR_THRESHOLD = 60.0  # rapidfuzz token_sort_ratio on normalised raw text
DETAILS = ("all", "summary", "classes", "lines", "links", "review")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- phrase normalisation
# Both the description and the key phrase go through the same rewrite, then all
# non-alphanumerics are dropped and we test substring containment.
_ABBREV = [  # catalog abbreviations -> long form
    (r"\bells?\b", "elbow"),
    (r"\bvlvs?\b", "valve"),
    (r"\bflgs?\b", "flange"),
    (r"\bgskts?\b", "gasket"),
    (r"\bspw\b", "spiral wound"),
    (r"\bmi\b", "malleable iron"),
    (r"\bcs\b", "carbon steel"),
    (r"\bfp\b", "full port"),
    (r"\bcplgs?\b", "coupling"),
    (r"\bred(ucer|ucing)?\b", "reduc"),
]
_SHORT = [  # spelled-out spec -> short form
    (r"\bschedule\b", "sch"),
    (r"\bclass\s*(\d+)\b", r"\1lb"),
    (r"\b(\d+)\s*(?:#|lbs?\b|pound\b)", r"\1lb"),
    (r"\bbutt[\s-]*weld(?:ed|ing)?\b", "bw"),
    (r"\b(?:threaded|thrd|thd|npt)\b", "thd"),
    (r"\bseamless\b", "smls"),
    (r"\bgalvani[sz]ed\b|\bgalv\b", "galv"),
]


def norm_phrase(s: str) -> str:
    s = s.lower()
    for pat, rep in _ABBREV + _SHORT:
        s = re.sub(pat, rep, s)
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "", s)


def mentions(desc: str, phrase: str) -> bool:
    """`phrase` may be "a|b" = either."""
    d = norm_phrase(desc)
    return any(norm_phrase(alt) in d for alt in phrase.split("|") if alt.strip())


def norm_raw(s: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(re.findall(r"\d+/\d+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?|[a-z]+", (s or "").lower()))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- pairing
def pair_lines(key: list[dict], pred: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[int, int, float]]:
    """Greedy best-first one-to-one pairing on raw-text similarity."""
    kn = [norm_raw(k.get("raw", "")) for k in key]
    pn = [norm_raw(p.get("raw", "")) for p in pred]
    scores = []
    for i, a in enumerate(kn):
        for j, b in enumerate(pn):
            sc = fuzz.token_sort_ratio(a, b)
            if sc >= PAIR_THRESHOLD:
                scores.append((sc, i, j))
    scores.sort(reverse=True)
    used_k, used_p, pairs = set(), set(), []
    for sc, i, j in scores:
        if i in used_k or j in used_p:
            continue
        used_k.add(i)
        used_p.add(j)
        pairs.append((i, j, sc))
    return pairs


def qty_ok(k: dict, p: dict) -> bool | None:
    tol = k.get("qty_tol")
    if tol is None:
        return None  # unscored
    kq, pq = k.get("qty"), p.get("qty")
    if kq is None or pq is None:
        return kq is None and pq is None
    if tol == 0:
        return float(kq) == float(pq)
    return abs(float(pq) - float(kq)) <= tol * abs(float(kq))


def uom_ok(k: dict, p: dict) -> bool:
    return (k.get("uom") or "EA") == (p.get("uom") or "EA")


def source_ok(k: dict, p: dict) -> bool:
    return (k.get("source") or "").strip().lower() == (p.get("source") or "").strip().lower()


def context(k: dict, p: dict) -> tuple[bool, list[str], list[str]]:
    desc = p.get("description") or ""
    missing = [m for m in k.get("must_mention", []) if not mentions(desc, m)]
    present = [m for m in k.get("must_not_mention", []) if mentions(desc, m)]
    return (not missing and not present), missing, present


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scoring
@dataclass
class Score:
    n_emails: int = 0
    class_correct: int = 0
    silent_losses: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    lost: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    phantom: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    confusions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    key_lines: int = 0
    pred_lines: int = 0
    paired: int = 0
    hallucinated: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    missed: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    qty_scored: int = 0
    qty_right: int = 0
    uom_right: int = 0
    source_right: int = 0
    ctx_right: int = 0
    line_fails: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    link_total: int = 0
    link_right: int = 0
    link_fails: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    rev_tp: int = 0
    rev_fp: int = 0
    rev_fn: int = 0
    review_fails: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    per_email: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def _pct(a: int, b: int) -> str:
    return f"{100 * a / b:.1f}% ({a}/{b})" if b else "n/a"


def score(key: dict, pred: dict, only: set[str] | None = None) -> Score:
    s = Score()
    for eid in sorted(key):
        if only and eid not in only:
            continue
        k = key[eid]
        p = pred.get(eid) or {"classification": None, "line_items": [], "needs_review": False}
        s.n_emails += 1
        rec: dict = {"lines": {}}
        kc, pc = k["classification"], p.get("classification")
        rec["class"] = [kc, pc]
        if kc == pc:
            s.class_correct += 1
        else:
            s.confusions.append(f"{eid}: key={kc} pred={pc}")
        if kc in REQUEST_KINDS and pc not in REQUEST_KINDS:
            s.lost.append(eid)
        if kc not in REQUEST_KINDS and pc in REQUEST_KINDS:
            s.phantom.append(eid)

        klines, plines = k.get("line_items", []), p.get("line_items") or []
        needs_action = bool(klines) or bool(k.get("needs_review"))
        if needs_action and not plines and not p.get("needs_review"):
            s.silent_losses.append(eid)

        s.key_lines += len(klines)
        s.pred_lines += len(plines)
        pairs = pair_lines(klines, plines)
        s.paired += len(pairs)
        pk = {i for i, _, _ in pairs}
        pp = {j for _, j, _ in pairs}
        for i, kl in enumerate(klines):
            if i not in pk:
                s.missed.append(f"{kl['id']}: {kl['raw']!r}")
                rec["lines"][kl["id"]] = "missed"
        for j, pl in enumerate(plines):
            if j not in pp:
                s.hallucinated.append(f"{eid}: {pl.get('raw')!r} [{pl.get('source')}]")
        rec["hallucinated"] = len(plines) - len(pp)

        for i, j, _ in pairs:
            kl, pl = klines[i], plines[j]
            q = qty_ok(kl, pl)
            u, src = uom_ok(kl, pl), source_ok(kl, pl)
            c, missing, present = context(kl, pl)
            if q is not None:
                s.qty_scored += 1
                s.qty_right += q
            s.uom_right += u
            s.source_right += src
            s.ctx_right += c
            probs = []
            if q is False:
                probs.append(f"qty {pl.get('qty')} != {kl.get('qty')}")
            if not u:
                probs.append(f"uom {pl.get('uom')} != {kl.get('uom')}")
            if not src:
                probs.append(f"source {pl.get('source')!r} != {kl.get('source')!r}")
            if missing:
                probs.append(f"missing {missing}")
            if present:
                probs.append(f"must-not {present}")
            rec["lines"][kl["id"]] = "ok" if not probs else "; ".join(probs)
            if probs:
                s.line_fails.append(
                    f"{kl['id']}: {'; '.join(probs)}\n    desc: {pl.get('description')!r}"
                )

        for f in ("revises", "duplicate_of"):
            kv, pv = k.get(f), p.get(f)
            if kv is None and pv is None:
                continue
            s.link_total += 1
            if kv == pv:
                s.link_right += 1
            else:
                s.link_fails.append(f"{eid}.{f}: key={kv} pred={pv}")

        kr, pr = bool(k.get("needs_review")), bool(p.get("needs_review"))
        s.rev_tp += kr and pr
        s.rev_fp += pr and not kr
        s.rev_fn += kr and not pr
        if kr != pr:
            s.review_fails.append(f"{eid}: key={kr} pred={pr} reason={p.get('review_reason')!r}")
        rec["needs_review"] = [kr, pr]
        s.per_email[eid] = rec
    return s


def headline(s: Score) -> dict:
    return {
        "silent_losses": len(s.silent_losses),
        "hallucinated_lines": len(s.hallucinated),
        "lost_requests": len(s.lost),
        "phantom_requests": len(s.phantom),
        "classification": _pct(s.class_correct, s.n_emails),
        "line_recall": _pct(s.paired, s.key_lines),
        "line_precision": _pct(s.paired, s.pred_lines),
        "qty": _pct(s.qty_right, s.qty_scored),
        "uom": _pct(s.uom_right, s.paired),
        "source": _pct(s.source_right, s.paired),
        "context_carried": _pct(s.ctx_right, s.paired),
        "links": _pct(s.link_right, s.link_total),
        "review_precision": _pct(s.rev_tp, s.rev_tp + s.rev_fp),
        "review_recall": _pct(s.rev_tp, s.rev_tp + s.rev_fn),
    }


def render(s: Score, detail: str) -> str:
    out = ["# Eval vs dev answer key", "", "| metric | value |", "|---|---|"]
    out += [f"| {k} | {v} |" for k, v in headline(s).items()]

    def section(name: str, title: str, items: list[str]) -> None:
        if detail in ("all", name) and items:
            out.extend(["", f"## {title} ({len(items)})", "", "```"])
            out.extend(items)
            out.append("```")

    section("classes", "Silent losses", s.silent_losses)
    section("classes", "Classification errors", s.confusions)
    section("lines", "Missed key lines", s.missed)
    section("lines", "Hallucinated / unpaired predicted lines", s.hallucinated)
    section("lines", "Paired-line field errors", s.line_fails)
    section("links", "Link errors", s.link_fails)
    section("review", "needs_review errors", s.review_fails)
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def diff(old: dict, new: dict) -> list[str]:
    changes = []
    for eid in sorted(set(old) | set(new)):
        o, n = old.get(eid, {}), new.get(eid, {})
        for f in ("class", "needs_review", "hallucinated"):
            if o.get(f) != n.get(f):
                changes.append(f"{eid}.{f}: {o.get(f)} -> {n.get(f)}")
        ol, nl = o.get("lines", {}), n.get("lines", {})
        for lid in sorted(set(ol) | set(nl)):
            if ol.get(lid) != nl.get(lid):
                changes.append(f"{lid}: {ol.get(lid)} -> {nl.get(lid)}")
    return changes


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
        sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("parsed", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--key", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_KEY)
    ap.add_argument("--detail", choices=DETAILS, default="summary", help="what to print to stdout")
    ap.add_argument("--emails", help="comma-separated email ids to score")
    ap.add_argument("--baseline", type=Path, help="previous eval.json to diff against")
    ap.add_argument("--reports", type=Path, default=ROOT / "reports")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    key = json.loads(a.key.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["emails"]
    pred = json.loads(a.parsed.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    only = set(a.emails.split(",")) if a.emails else None
    s = score(key, pred, only)

    baseline = None
    if a.baseline and a.baseline.exists():
        baseline = json.loads(a.baseline.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("per_email", {})

    a.reports.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not only:  # only full runs overwrite the reports
        (a.reports / "eval.md").write_text(render(s, "all"), encoding="utf-8")
        (a.reports / "eval.json").write_text(
            json.dumps({"headline": headline(s), "per_email": s.per_email}, indent=1) + "\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
    print(render(s, a.detail))
    if baseline is not None:
        changes = diff(baseline, s.per_email)
        print(f"## Changes vs baseline ({len(changes)})")
        print("\n".join(changes) or "(none)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Score parsed.json against the dev answer key, following data/README.md "What we grade".

    python eval/eval.py parsed.json
    python eval/eval.py parsed.json --detail lines          # per-line failures only
    python eval/eval.py parsed.json --emails E003,E007      # restrict to some emails
    python eval/eval.py parsed.json --baseline reports/eval.json   # what changed since last run

Writes reports/eval.md (human) and reports/eval.json (per-email/per-line outcomes, for diffs).
This is the ONLY code in the repo allowed to read answer_key.json.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from rapidfuzz import fuzz

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DEFAULT_KEY = ROOT / "data" / "dev" / "answer_key.json"
REQUEST_KINDS = {"rfq", "rfq_revision", "purchase_order"}
PAIR_THRESHOLD = 60.0  # rapidfuzz token_sort_ratio on normalised raw text
DETAILS = ("all", "summary", "classes", "lines", "links", "review")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- phrase normalisation
# Both the description and the key phrase go through the same rewrite, then all
# non-alphanumerics are dropped and we test substring containment.
_ABBREV = [  # catalog abbreviations -> long form
    (r"\bells?\b", "elbow"),
    (r"\bvlvs?\b", "valve"),
    (r"\bflgs?\b", "flange"),
    (r"\bgskts?\b", "gasket"),
    (r"\bspw\b", "spiral wound"),
    (r"\bmi\b", "malleable iron"),
    (r"\bcs\b", "carbon steel"),
    (r"\bfp\b", "full port"),
    (r"\bcplgs?\b", "coupling"),
    (r"\bred(ucer|ucing)?\b", "reduc"),
]
_SHORT = [  # spelled-out spec -> short form
    (r"\bschedule\b", "sch"),
    (r"\bclass\s*(\d+)\b", r"\1lb"),
    (r"\b(\d+)\s*(?:#|lbs?\b|pound\b)", r"\1lb"),
    (r"\bbutt[\s-]*weld(?:ed|ing)?\b", "bw"),
    (r"\b(?:threaded|thrd|thd|npt)\b", "thd"),
    (r"\bseamless\b", "smls"),
    (r"\bgalvani[sz]ed\b|\bgalv\b", "galv"),
]


def norm_phrase(s: str) -> str:
    s = s.lower()
    for pat, rep in _ABBREV + _SHORT:
        s = re.sub(pat, rep, s)
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "", s)


def mentions(desc: str, phrase: str) -> bool:
    """`phrase` may be "a|b" = either."""
    d = norm_phrase(desc)
    return any(norm_phrase(alt) in d for alt in phrase.split("|") if alt.strip())


def norm_raw(s: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(re.findall(r"\d+/\d+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?|[a-z]+", (s or "").lower()))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- pairing
def pair_lines(key: list[dict], pred: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[int, int, float]]:
    """Greedy best-first one-to-one pairing on raw-text similarity."""
    kn = [norm_raw(k.get("raw", "")) for k in key]
    pn = [norm_raw(p.get("raw", "")) for p in pred]
    scores = []
    for i, a in enumerate(kn):
        for j, b in enumerate(pn):
            sc = fuzz.token_sort_ratio(a, b)
            if sc >= PAIR_THRESHOLD:
                scores.append((sc, i, j))
    scores.sort(reverse=True)
    used_k, used_p, pairs = set(), set(), []
    for sc, i, j in scores:
        if i in used_k or j in used_p:
            continue
        used_k.add(i)
        used_p.add(j)
        pairs.append((i, j, sc))
    return pairs


def qty_ok(k: dict, p: dict) -> bool | None:
    tol = k.get("qty_tol")
    if tol is None:
        return None  # unscored
    kq, pq = k.get("qty"), p.get("qty")
    if kq is None or pq is None:
        return kq is None and pq is None
    if tol == 0:
        return float(kq) == float(pq)
    return abs(float(pq) - float(kq)) <= tol * abs(float(kq))


def uom_ok(k: dict, p: dict) -> bool:
    return (k.get("uom") or "EA") == (p.get("uom") or "EA")


def source_ok(k: dict, p: dict) -> bool:
    return (k.get("source") or "").strip().lower() == (p.get("source") or "").strip().lower()


def context(k: dict, p: dict) -> tuple[bool, list[str], list[str]]:
    desc = p.get("description") or ""
    missing = [m for m in k.get("must_mention", []) if not mentions(desc, m)]
    present = [m for m in k.get("must_not_mention", []) if mentions(desc, m)]
    return (not missing and not present), missing, present


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scoring
@dataclass
class Score:
    n_emails: int = 0
    class_correct: int = 0
    silent_losses: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    lost: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    phantom: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    confusions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    key_lines: int = 0
    pred_lines: int = 0
    paired: int = 0
    hallucinated: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    missed: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    qty_scored: int = 0
    qty_right: int = 0
    uom_right: int = 0
    source_right: int = 0
    ctx_right: int = 0
    line_fails: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    link_total: int = 0
    link_right: int = 0
    link_fails: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    rev_tp: int = 0
    rev_fp: int = 0
    rev_fn: int = 0
    review_fails: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    per_email: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def _pct(a: int, b: int) -> str:
    return f"{100 * a / b:.1f}% ({a}/{b})" if b else "n/a"


def score(key: dict, pred: dict, only: set[str] | None = None) -> Score:
    s = Score()
    for eid in sorted(key):
        if only and eid not in only:
            continue
        k = key[eid]
        p = pred.get(eid) or {"classification": None, "line_items": [], "needs_review": False}
        s.n_emails += 1
        rec: dict = {"lines": {}}
        kc, pc = k["classification"], p.get("classification")
        rec["class"] = [kc, pc]
        if kc == pc:
            s.class_correct += 1
        else:
            s.confusions.append(f"{eid}: key={kc} pred={pc}")
        if kc in REQUEST_KINDS and pc not in REQUEST_KINDS:
            s.lost.append(eid)
        if kc not in REQUEST_KINDS and pc in REQUEST_KINDS:
            s.phantom.append(eid)

        klines, plines = k.get("line_items", []), p.get("line_items") or []
        needs_action = bool(klines) or bool(k.get("needs_review"))
        if needs_action and not plines and not p.get("needs_review"):
            s.silent_losses.append(eid)

        s.key_lines += len(klines)
        s.pred_lines += len(plines)
        pairs = pair_lines(klines, plines)
        s.paired += len(pairs)
        pk = {i for i, _, _ in pairs}
        pp = {j for _, j, _ in pairs}
        for i, kl in enumerate(klines):
            if i not in pk:
                s.missed.append(f"{kl['id']}: {kl['raw']!r}")
                rec["lines"][kl["id"]] = "missed"
        for j, pl in enumerate(plines):
            if j not in pp:
                s.hallucinated.append(f"{eid}: {pl.get('raw')!r} [{pl.get('source')}]")
        rec["hallucinated"] = len(plines) - len(pp)

        for i, j, _ in pairs:
            kl, pl = klines[i], plines[j]
            q = qty_ok(kl, pl)
            u, src = uom_ok(kl, pl), source_ok(kl, pl)
            c, missing, present = context(kl, pl)
            if q is not None:
                s.qty_scored += 1
                s.qty_right += q
            s.uom_right += u
            s.source_right += src
            s.ctx_right += c
            probs = []
            if q is False:
                probs.append(f"qty {pl.get('qty')} != {kl.get('qty')}")
            if not u:
                probs.append(f"uom {pl.get('uom')} != {kl.get('uom')}")
            if not src:
                probs.append(f"source {pl.get('source')!r} != {kl.get('source')!r}")
            if missing:
                probs.append(f"missing {missing}")
            if present:
                probs.append(f"must-not {present}")
            rec["lines"][kl["id"]] = "ok" if not probs else "; ".join(probs)
            if probs:
                s.line_fails.append(
                    f"{kl['id']}: {'; '.join(probs)}\n    desc: {pl.get('description')!r}"
                )

        for f in ("revises", "duplicate_of"):
            kv, pv = k.get(f), p.get(f)
            if kv is None and pv is None:
                continue
            s.link_total += 1
            if kv == pv:
                s.link_right += 1
            else:
                s.link_fails.append(f"{eid}.{f}: key={kv} pred={pv}")

        kr, pr = bool(k.get("needs_review")), bool(p.get("needs_review"))
        s.rev_tp += kr and pr
        s.rev_fp += pr and not kr
        s.rev_fn += kr and not pr
        if kr != pr:
            s.review_fails.append(f"{eid}: key={kr} pred={pr} reason={p.get('review_reason')!r}")
        rec["needs_review"] = [kr, pr]
        s.per_email[eid] = rec
    return s


def headline(s: Score) -> dict:
    return {
        "silent_losses": len(s.silent_losses),
        "hallucinated_lines": len(s.hallucinated),
        "lost_requests": len(s.lost),
        "phantom_requests": len(s.phantom),
        "classification": _pct(s.class_correct, s.n_emails),
        "line_recall": _pct(s.paired, s.key_lines),
        "line_precision": _pct(s.paired, s.pred_lines),
        "qty": _pct(s.qty_right, s.qty_scored),
        "uom": _pct(s.uom_right, s.paired),
        "source": _pct(s.source_right, s.paired),
        "context_carried": _pct(s.ctx_right, s.paired),
        "links": _pct(s.link_right, s.link_total),
        "review_precision": _pct(s.rev_tp, s.rev_tp + s.rev_fp),
        "review_recall": _pct(s.rev_tp, s.rev_tp + s.rev_fn),
    }


def render(s: Score, detail: str) -> str:
    out = ["# Eval vs dev answer key", "", "| metric | value |", "|---|---|"]
    out += [f"| {k} | {v} |" for k, v in headline(s).items()]

    def section(name: str, title: str, items: list[str]) -> None:
        if detail in ("all", name) and items:
            out.extend(["", f"## {title} ({len(items)})", "", "```"])
            out.extend(items)
            out.append("```")

    section("classes", "Silent losses", s.silent_losses)
    section("classes", "Classification errors", s.confusions)
    section("lines", "Missed key lines", s.missed)
    section("lines", "Hallucinated / unpaired predicted lines", s.hallucinated)
    section("lines", "Paired-line field errors", s.line_fails)
    section("links", "Link errors", s.link_fails)
    section("review", "needs_review errors", s.review_fails)
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def diff(old: dict, new: dict) -> list[str]:
    changes = []
    for eid in sorted(set(old) | set(new)):
        o, n = old.get(eid, {}), new.get(eid, {})
        for f in ("class", "needs_review", "hallucinated"):
            if o.get(f) != n.get(f):
                changes.append(f"{eid}.{f}: {o.get(f)} -> {n.get(f)}")
        ol, nl = o.get("lines", {}), n.get("lines", {})
        for lid in sorted(set(ol) | set(nl)):
            if ol.get(lid) != nl.get(lid):
                changes.append(f"{lid}: {ol.get(lid)} -> {nl.get(lid)}")
    return changes


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
        sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("parsed", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--key", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_KEY)
    ap.add_argument("--detail", choices=DETAILS, default="summary", help="what to print to stdout")
    ap.add_argument("--emails", help="comma-separated email ids to score")
    ap.add_argument("--baseline", type=Path, help="previous eval.json to diff against")
    ap.add_argument("--reports", type=Path, default=ROOT / "reports")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    key = json.loads(a.key.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["emails"]
    pred = json.loads(a.parsed.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    only = set(a.emails.split(",")) if a.emails else None
    s = score(key, pred, only)

    baseline = None
    if a.baseline and a.baseline.exists():
        baseline = json.loads(a.baseline.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("per_email", {})

    a.reports.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not only:  # only full runs overwrite the reports
        (a.reports / "eval.md").write_text(render(s, "all"), encoding="utf-8")
        (a.reports / "eval.json").write_text(
            json.dumps({"headline": headline(s), "per_email": s.per_email}, indent=1) + "\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
    print(render(s, a.detail))
    if baseline is not None:
        changes = diff(baseline, s.per_email)
        print(f"## Changes vs baseline ({len(changes)})")
        print("\n".join(changes) or "(none)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

**Scorer check:** I fed the answer key back in as if it were our output (descriptions built from each line's `must_mention` phrases). There is one more lost request than silent losses because one request email expects no lines, probably the duplicate.

**What I added**
- **[eval/eval.py](eval/eval.py)**: the only file that reads `answer_key.json`.
  - **Metrics:** it reports the README's headline numbers first (silent losses, hallucinated lines, lost and phantom requests), then classification, line recall and precision, qty/uom/source on paired lines, context carried, links, and needs_review precision and recall.
  - **Line pairing:** our lines are paired one-to-one with the key's by similarity of the `raw` text, ignoring case and punctuation. Pairs below a score of 60 don't count, and the best-scoring pairs are taken first.
  - **Context check:** before comparing descriptions, both sides are rewritten into one form for the spellings the README treats as equal (Sch/Schedule, 150#/150 lb/Class 150, BW, NPT, SMLS, galv, ELL, VLV, FLG and the rest).
  - **Output:** it writes `reports/eval.md` (readable) and `reports/eval.json` (per-email and per-line results).
  - **Options:** `--baseline reports/eval.json` lists which emails and lines changed since the last run, which you asked for whenever a number drops. `--detail classes|lines|links|review` narrows the printout, and `--emails` scores a subset (a subset run doesn't overwrite the reports).
- **[tests/test_eval.py](tests/test_eval.py)**: tests the spelling rules, pairing, qty tolerance and the silent-loss/phantom rules, using made-up strings only. `pytest -q`: 6 passed.

**Known limits of my scorer:**
- My pairing threshold and greedy matching are guesses at what the graders do. Our numbers could differ from theirs at the edges.
- Phrases are compared as substrings with spaces removed, so "sch40" would also match inside "sch400". That's acceptable here.
- "red" is read as "reducer"; I'll watch for false hits on that.

def describe(e: Email) -> str:
    """Human-readable dump of a parsed email, for inspection and debugging."""
    h = e.headers
    out = [
        f"===== {e.id}",
        f"from: {h.get('from')}  internal={e.internal}",
        f"subject: {h.get('subject')}",
        f"date: {e.date}  message_id: {h.get('message_id')}",
        f"in_reply_to: {h.get('in_reply_to')}  references: {h.get('references')}",
        f"body from: {e.body_kind}",
        "--- current ---",
        e.body or "(empty)",
    ]
    if e.forwarded:
        out += ["--- forwarded ---", e.forwarded]
    if e.quoted:
        out += ["--- quoted history ---", e.quoted]
    for a in e.attachments:
        alt = e.image_alts.get(a.content_id or "") or e.image_alts.get(a.filename, "")
        out.append(
            f"--- attachment: {a.filename} [{a.mime}] {len(a.data)} bytes"
            f"{' inline' if a.inline else ''}{f' cid={a.content_id}' if a.content_id else ''}"
            f"{f' alt={alt!r}' if alt else ''}"
        )
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"

Later steps replace `process_email` with mime -> extract -> prompt -> cache/llm -> validate.

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.models import Result

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def process_email(path: Path) -> Result:
    """Stub: reads the file (so unreadable files fail here) and returns an empty `other`."""
    path.read_bytes()
    return Result(classification="other")


def failed_result(reason: str) -> Result:
    """Entry for an email we could not process at all.

    We don't know what it is, so it is treated as a possible request and flagged: a human
    looking at a non-request costs minutes; a silently dropped request costs a customer.
    """
    return Result(classification="rfq", needs_review=True, review_reason=reason)


def process_inbox(emails_dir: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for path in sorted(emails_dir.glob("*.eml")):
        try:
            result = process_email(path)
        except Exception as e:  # one bad email never takes down the run
            log.exception("failed on %s", path.name)
            result = failed_result(f"could not process email: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        out[path.stem] = result.to_json()
    return out

"""Command line: `rfq parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json` (or `python -m rfq parse ...`)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.pipeline import process_inbox


def _write_json_atomic(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    tmp.replace(path)


def cmd_parse(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    emails_dir = Path(args.emails)
    if not emails_dir.is_dir():
        print(f"--emails: not a directory: {emails_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    results = process_inbox(emails_dir)
    _write_json_atomic(Path(args.out), results)
    print(f"wrote {len(results)} emails to {args.out}")
    return 0


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="rfq", description="Ridgeline RFQ inbox parser")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("parse", help="parse every .eml in a directory")
    p.add_argument("--emails", required=True, help="directory of .eml files")
    p.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output JSON path")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_parse)
    return ap


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
        sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    return args.func(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Step 3 is done: every dev email now parses into its current text, forwarded text, quoted history and attachments, and all 24 splits came out right when I checked them. `pytest -q` passes (19 tests). `parse` still returns the placeholder result, so the eval is unchanged with no differences from the baseline, as expected.

**What I added**
- **[rfq/mime.py](rfq/mime.py)**: `parse_message(bytes, id)` turns each email into one object.
  - **History split:** it recognises `On … wrote:` (including when it wraps onto a second line), Outlook's `From:/Sent:/To:/Subject:` block, `-----Original Message-----`, Gmail's `---------- Forwarded message ---------` / `Begin forwarded message:`, and runs of `>` lines. The `>` prefixes are removed from quoted text.
  - **Forward vs reply:** Outlook writes `-----Original Message-----` for both. I treat it as a forward only when the subject starts with `FW:`/`Fwd:`. If a forwarded email has its own reply history, that part goes to quoted.
  - **Bodies:** the HTML part is used when it contains a table (each row becomes one line, cells joined by ` | `) or when there's no plain text; otherwise the plain text is used. HTML quote blocks become `>` lines, so the same split rules apply.
  - **Attachments:** inline images keep their content IDs, and their HTML `alt` text is collected even when the plain-text body is used. A nested email (E013's bounce) becomes an attachment that can be parsed again.
  - **Bad input:** unreadable character sets and dates fall back instead of raising an error.
- **`rfq inspect <file|dir> [--out f]`**: prints how each email was split, with no model calls. It's useful for debugging and for the live change in the interview.
- **[rfq/models.py](rfq/models.py)**: the email object gained `forwarded`, `sender`, `internal`, `date`, `body_kind` and `image_alts`.
- **[tests/test_mime.py](tests/test_mime.py)**: 12 tests on made-up emails. One failure along the way was a mistake in my test, not the code: the `>` it found was from an email address.

**Fix found by inspecting:** E013's bounce comes from `MAILER-DAEMON@mx1.ridgeline-supply.example` and was marked as one of our reps. Now only the exact `@ridgeline-supply.example` domain counts as internal, and a test covers it.

**Decisions for later steps, flagged now:**
- **Quoted history is kept, not dropped.** E004 ("line 2 is now 14") and E020 ("go ahead with items 1, 2 and 4") can't produce a complete order without the quoted list. So quoted lines will be shown to the model clearly marked, and allowed as a line source only for `rfq_revision` and `purchase_order`.
- **Forwards from customers.** Forwarded text is separated for any sender, not only our reps. Whether a customer forwarding someone else's list counts as a request gets decided in the prompt and validation steps.
- **Two problems I can already see:**
  - E017 says "BOM attached" but has only a logo image, so it should be flagged for review because the attachment is missing.
  - E010's pasted screenshot can be told apart from its logo by the alt text and image size.

"""The email's own text -> one Doc with addressable lines.

Row ids: body!B<n> current message, body!F<n> forwarded content, body!Q<n> quoted history.
All three have source "body"; the prefix tells later steps which part a line came from.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from rfq.config import MAX_TEXT_LINES
from rfq.models import Doc, Email, Line


def _lines(text: str, prefix: str) -> list[Line]:
    out = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        t = raw.strip()
        if t:
            out.append(Line(row_id=f"body!{prefix}{len(out) + 1}", text=t))
    return out


def extract_body(email: Email) -> Doc:
    doc = Doc(source="body", kind="body")
    for text, prefix in ((email.body, "B"), (email.forwarded, "F"), (email.quoted, "Q")):
        doc.lines += _lines(text, prefix)
    if len(doc.lines) > MAX_TEXT_LINES:
        doc.lines = doc.lines[:MAX_TEXT_LINES]
        doc.truncated = True
        doc.notes.append(f"body truncated to {MAX_TEXT_LINES} lines")
    if email.body_kind == "none":
        doc.notes.append("email has no text body")
    return doc

"""CSV / TSV -> Doc. Row ids: <file>!R<n> (1-based, header included)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io

from rfq.config import MAX_ROWS_PER_SHEET
from rfq.extractors.common import decode_text, row_text
from rfq.models import Doc, Line


def extract_csv(name: str, data: bytes) -> Doc:
    doc = Doc(source=name, kind="csv")
    text = decode_text(data)
    try:
        dialect = csv.Sniffer().sniff(text[:4096], delimiters=",;\t|")
    except csv.Error:
        dialect = csv.excel_tab if name.lower().endswith(".tsv") else csv.excel
    for i, row in enumerate(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text), dialect), start=1):
        cells = [" ".join(c.split()) for c in row]
        if not any(cells):
            continue
        if len(doc.lines) >= MAX_ROWS_PER_SHEET:
            doc.truncated = True
            doc.notes.append(f"truncated at {MAX_ROWS_PER_SHEET} rows")
            break
        doc.lines.append(Line(row_id=f"{name}!R{i}", text=row_text(cells), cells=cells))
    return doc

"""The email's own text -> one Doc with addressable lines.

Row ids: body!B<n> current message, body!F<n> forwarded content, body!Q<n> quoted history.
All three have source "body"; the prefix tells later steps which part a line came from.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from rfq.config import MAX_TEXT_LINES
from rfq.models import Doc, Email, Line


def _lines(text: str, prefix: str) -> list[Line]:
    out = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        t = raw.strip()
        if t:
            out.append(Line(row_id=f"body!{prefix}{len(out) + 1}", text=t))
    return out


def extract_body(email: Email) -> Doc:
    doc = Doc(source="body", kind="body")
    for text, prefix in ((email.body, "B"), (email.forwarded, "F"), (email.quoted, "Q")):
        doc.lines += _lines(text, prefix)
    if len(doc.lines) > MAX_TEXT_LINES:
        doc.lines = doc.lines[:MAX_TEXT_LINES]
        doc.truncated = True
        doc.notes.append(f"body truncated to {MAX_TEXT_LINES} lines")
    if email.body_kind == "none":
        doc.notes.append("email has no text body")
    return doc
