"""Model answer -> Result: code owns raw/qty/uom and the drop rules (synthetic data)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from rfq.models import Doc, Email, Line
from rfq.schema import Extraction
from rfq.validate import build_result, normalize_uom


def _ln(row_id, raw, desc="d", qty=None, uom=None, image=None):
    return {"row_id": row_id, "image": image, "raw": raw, "description": desc, "qty": qty, "uom": uom}


def _ans(kind, lines, **kw):
    body = {"kind": kind, "lines": lines, "sheet_decisions": kw.get("sheets", []),
            "needs_review": kw.get("review", False), "review_reason": kw.get("reason"), "rationale": "r"}
    return Extraction.model_validate({"result": body})


EMAIL = Email(id="T", headers={}, body="")
BODY = Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[
    Line("body!B1", "Please quote: 10 of the 1/2 90s and 6 tees same size"),
    Line("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve"),
    Line("body!Q1", "8 ea 3in cap"),
])
SHEET = Doc(source="bom.xlsx", kind="xlsx", lines=[
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R1", "ALL SCH 40", cells=["ALL SCH 40"]),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R2", "Item | Qty | UOM | Size", cells=["Item", "Qty", "UOM", "Size"]),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R3", 'Tee | 12 | EA | 2"', cells=["Tee", "12", "EA", '2"']),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R4", 'Cap | 3 | EA | 2"', cells=["Cap", "3", "EA", '2"'], struck=True),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R5", 'Pipe | 40 ft | | 2"', cells=["Pipe", "40 ft", "", '2"']),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev A!R3", 'Tee | 8 | EA | 2"', cells=["Tee", "8", "EA", '2"']),
])
DOCS = [BODY, SHEET]


def test_table_row_raw_qty_uom_come_from_cells_not_model() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [_ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R3", "tee twelve", qty=99, uom="FT")]))
    li = r.line_items[0]
    assert (li.raw, li.qty, li.uom, li.source) == ('Tee | 12 | EA | 2"', 12, "EA", "bom.xlsx")


def test_unit_inside_qty_cell() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [_ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R5", "pipe")]))
    assert (r.line_items[0].qty, r.line_items[0].uom) == (40, "FT")


def test_fragment_kept_when_grounded_else_whole_line() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [
        _ln("body!B1", "10 of the 1/2 90s", qty=10),
        _ln("body!B1", "6 tees same size", qty=6),
        _ln("body!B2", "four gate valves 2 inch", qty=4, uom="EA"),  # not a fragment of the line
    ]))
    assert [li.raw for li in r.line_items] == ["10 of the 1/2 90s", "6 tees same size", "4 ea 2in gate valve"]


def test_unknown_struck_and_quoted_rows_dropped_for_rfq() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [
        _ln("body!B9", "invented"), _ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R4", "cap"), _ln("body!Q1", "8 ea 3in cap"),
        _ln("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve", qty=4),
    ]))
    assert [li.raw for li in r.line_items] == ["4 ea 2in gate valve"]


def test_quoted_rows_allowed_for_revision_and_po() -> None:
    for kind in ("rfq_revision", "purchase_order"):
        r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans(kind, [_ln("body!Q1", "8 ea 3in cap", qty=8)]), parent="P1")
        assert [li.raw for li in r.line_items] == ["8 ea 3in cap"]
        assert r.revises == ("P1" if kind == "rfq_revision" else None)


def test_versions_keep_only_newest_sheet_and_unclear_flags() -> None:
    lines = [_ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R3", "tee"), _ln("bom.xlsx!Rev A!R3", "tee")]
    sd = {"file": "bom.xlsx", "relation": "versions", "sheets_used": ["Rev B"], "why": "Rev B is newer"}
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", lines, sheets=[sd]))
    assert [li.qty for li in r.line_items] == [12] and not r.needs_review
    sd_unclear = {**sd, "relation": "unclear", "sheets_used": ["Rev B", "Rev A"]}
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", lines, sheets=[sd_unclear]))
    assert r.needs_review and "sections or versions" in r.review_reason and len(r.line_items) == 2


def test_image_lines_keep_model_raw_and_map_source() -> None:
    img = Doc(source="scan.pdf", kind="pdf")
    from rfq.models import ImagePart

    img.images = [ImagePart("scan.pdf page 2", b"x", 1, 1)]
    r = build_result(EMAIL, [BODY, img], _ans("rfq", [_ln(None, "6 - 4in blind flg", qty=6, image="scan.pdf page 2")]))
    assert (r.line_items[0].raw, r.line_items[0].source) == ("6 - 4in blind flg", "scan.pdf")


def test_no_items_kinds_have_no_lines_and_no_review() -> None:
    ans = Extraction.model_validate({"result": {"kind": "vendor_quote", "rationale": "supplier pricing"}})
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, ans, problems=["x.pdf: broken"])
    assert r.classification == "vendor_quote" and r.line_items == [] and not r.needs_review


def test_review_reasons_merge_and_silent_loss_guard() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", []))
    assert r.needs_review and "no line items" in r.review_reason
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [_ln("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve")], review=True,
                                       reason="BOM not attached"), problems=["a.pdf: password-protected"])
    assert r.needs_review and "BOM not attached" in r.review_reason and "password" in r.review_reason


def test_no_answer_is_flagged_request() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, None, model_error="model unavailable")
    assert r.classification == "rfq" and r.needs_review and "model unavailable" in r.review_reason


def test_normalize_uom() -> None:
    assert [normalize_uom(x) for x in ("jts", "Feet", "rolls", "PR", "bogus", None)] == ["EA", "FT", "RL", "PR", None, None]

"""Model-call tests with a fake OpenAI client (no network, no key)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import openai
import pytest

from rfq.cache import Cache
from rfq.llm import Extractor
from rfq.models import Doc, Email, ImagePart, Line
from rfq.prompt import build_messages
from rfq.schema import response_format

GOOD = {"result": {"kind": "rfq", "lines": [
    {"row_id": "body!B1", "image": None, "raw": "4 ea 2in tee", "description": "2in tee", "qty": 4, "uom": "EA"}],
    "sheet_decisions": [], "needs_review": False, "review_reason": None, "rationale": "asks for prices"}}


def _resp(content: str, finish: str = "stop", refusal=None, tokens=(1000, 200)):
    msg = SimpleNamespace(content=content, refusal=refusal)
    usage = SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=tokens[0], completion_tokens=tokens[1],
                            prompt_tokens_details=SimpleNamespace(cached_tokens=0))
    return SimpleNamespace(choices=[SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason=finish)], usage=usage)


class FakeClient:
    """Replays a script of responses / exceptions; records every request."""

    def __init__(self, script):
        self.script = list(script)
        self.requests: list[dict] = []
        self.chat = SimpleNamespace(completions=SimpleNamespace(create=self._create))

    def _create(self, **kw):
        self.requests.append(kw)
        item = self.script.pop(0)
        if isinstance(item, Exception):
            raise item
        return item


def _email() -> tuple[Email, list[Doc]]:
    e = Email(id="T1", headers={"subject": "RFQ"}, body="4 ea 2in tee")
    return e, [Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[Line("body!B1", "4 ea 2in tee")])]


def _transient() -> Exception:
    req = openai._base_client.httpx.Request("POST", "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions") \
        if hasattr(openai._base_client, "httpx") else None
    return openai.APITimeoutError(request=req)


def _ex(tmp_path: Path, script) -> tuple[Extractor, FakeClient]:
    client = FakeClient(script)
    return Extractor(model="gpt-4.1", cache=Cache(tmp_path / "cache"), client=client, wait_max_s=0.01), client


def test_valid_answer_is_cached_and_second_run_makes_no_call(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, client = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    e, docs = _email()
    first = ex.run(e, docs)
    assert first.extraction and not first.cache_hit and first.live_calls == 1
    assert first.cost_usd == pytest.approx((1000 * 2.0 + 200 * 8.0) / 1e6)
    second = ex.run(e, docs)  # script is empty now: any call would raise IndexError
    assert second.cache_hit and second.live_calls == 0 and second.live_cost_usd == 0
    assert second.cost_usd == first.cost_usd  # cost to produce is still reported
    assert len(client.requests) == 1


def test_request_uses_strict_schema_and_temperature_zero(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, client = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    ex.run(*_email())
    req = client.requests[0]
    assert req["response_format"] == response_format() and req["temperature"] == 0
    assert req["messages"][0]["role"] == "system"


def test_invalid_then_repaired(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, client = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp('{"result": {"kind": "rfq"}}'), _resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction and out.live_calls == 2
    assert "corrected JSON" in client.requests[1]["messages"][-1]["content"]


def test_invalid_twice_is_error_and_not_cached(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp("not json"), _resp("still not json")])
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction is None and "rejected" in out.error and not out.retryable
    assert not list((tmp_path / "cache").glob("*.json")) if (tmp_path / "cache").exists() else True


def test_transient_errors_are_retried(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_transient(), _transient(), _resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction and out.live_calls == 3


def test_transient_errors_exhausted_is_retryable_failure(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_transient()] * 4)
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction is None and out.retryable and out.live_calls == 4


def test_refusal_and_length_are_errors(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp("", refusal="no")])
    assert "refused" in ex.run(*_email()).error
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp('{"result":', finish="length")])
    assert "too long" in ex.run(*_email()).error


def test_no_key_and_cache_miss_is_flagged_not_crash(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex = Extractor(model="gpt-4.1", cache=Cache(tmp_path / "cache"))  # offline via conftest
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction is None and out.retryable and "no cached response" in out.error


def test_cache_key_changes_with_content_model_and_prompt_version(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp(json.dumps(GOOD))] * 3)
    e, docs = _email()
    k1 = ex.run(e, docs).key
    docs2 = [Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[Line("body!B1", "5 ea 2in tee")])]
    assert ex.run(e, docs2).key != k1
    import rfq.llm as llm

    monkeypatch.setattr(llm, "PROMPT_VERSION", "p-test")
    assert ex.run(e, docs).key != k1


def test_images_go_as_vision_parts() -> None:
    e = Email(id="T2", headers={}, body="see photo")
    docs = [Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[Line("body!B1", "see photo")]),

from rfq.schema import Extraction
from rfq.validate import build_result, normalize_uom


def _ln(row_id, raw, desc="d", qty=None, uom=None, image=None):
    return {"row_id": row_id, "image": image, "raw": raw, "description": desc, "qty": qty, "uom": uom}


def _ans(kind, lines, **kw):
    body = {"kind": kind, "lines": lines, "sheet_decisions": kw.get("sheets", []),
            "needs_review": kw.get("review", False), "review_reason": kw.get("reason"), "rationale": "r"}

EMAIL = Email(id="T", headers={}, body="")
BODY = Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[
    Line("body!B1", "Please quote: 10 of the 1/2 90s and 6 tees same size"),
    Line("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve"),
    Line("body!Q1", "8 ea 3in cap"),
])
SHEET = Doc(source="bom.xlsx", kind="xlsx", lines=[
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R1", "ALL SCH 40", cells=["ALL SCH 40"]),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R2", "Item | Qty | UOM | Size", cells=["Item", "Qty", "UOM", "Size"]),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R3", 'Tee | 12 | EA | 2"', cells=["Tee", "12", "EA", '2"']),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R4", 'Cap | 3 | EA | 2"', cells=["Cap", "3", "EA", '2"'], struck=True),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R5", 'Pipe | 40 ft | | 2"', cells=["Pipe", "40 ft", "", '2"']),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev A!R3", 'Tee | 8 | EA | 2"', cells=["Tee", "8", "EA", '2"']),
])
DOCS = [BODY, SHEET]


def test_table_row_raw_qty_uom_come_from_cells_not_model() -> None:

    li = r.line_items[0]
    assert (li.raw, li.qty, li.uom, li.source) == ('Tee | 12 | EA | 2"', 12, "EA", "bom.xlsx")

"""Per-run logs and the cost report.

runs/<run_id>/calls.jsonl     one line per email: cache hit?, tokens, $, latency, error
runs/<run_id>/failures.jsonl  emails that could not get a model answer, with `retryable`
runs/latest/                  copy of the most recent run (committed)
reports/cost.md               totals and per-email table
Never contains the API key or request content.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.config import REPORTS_DIR, RUNS_DIR


class RunLog:
    def __init__(self, model: str, runs_dir: Path = RUNS_DIR, reports_dir: Path = REPORTS_DIR) -> None:
        self.model = model
        self.run_id = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
        self.dir = runs_dir / self.run_id
        self.dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.runs_dir = runs_dir
        self.reports_dir = reports_dir
        self.rows: list[dict] = []

    def _append(self, name: str, row: dict) -> None:
        with (self.dir / name).open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

    def record(self, email_id: str, outcome=None, *, skipped: str | None = None, n_images: int = 0) -> None:
        if outcome is None:
            row = {"email": email_id, "skipped": skipped, "live_calls": 0, "cache_hit": False,
                   "input_tokens": 0, "cached_input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0,
                   "cost_usd": 0.0, "live_cost_usd": 0.0, "latency_s": 0.0, "images": 0, "error": None}
        else:
            row = {
                "email": email_id, "skipped": None, "model": self.model,
                "cache_hit": outcome.cache_hit, "live_calls": outcome.live_calls,
                "input_tokens": outcome.usage.input_tokens,
                "cached_input_tokens": outcome.usage.cached_input_tokens,
                "output_tokens": outcome.usage.output_tokens,
                "cost_usd": outcome.cost_usd, "live_cost_usd": outcome.live_cost_usd,
                "latency_s": outcome.latency_s, "images": n_images,
                "prompt_truncated": outcome.prompt_truncated, "error": outcome.error,
            }
            if outcome.error:
                self._append("failures.jsonl", {"email": email_id, "error": outcome.error,
                                                "retryable": outcome.retryable})
        self.rows.append(row)
        self._append("calls.jsonl", row)

    def finish(self) -> Path:
        report = self.render()
        self.reports_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (self.reports_dir / "cost.md").write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
        (self.dir / "cost.md").write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
        latest = self.runs_dir / "latest"
        if latest.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(latest)
        shutil.copytree(self.dir, latest)
        return self.reports_dir / "cost.md"

    def render(self) -> str:
        rows = self.rows
        modelled = [r for r in rows if not r.get("skipped")]
        tot = {k: sum(r.get(k, 0) or 0 for r in rows) for k in
               ("live_calls", "input_tokens", "cached_input_tokens", "output_tokens", "cost_usd", "live_cost_usd")}
        hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("cache_hit"))
        errors = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("error"))
        n = max(len(modelled), 1)
        out = [
            "# Cost report", "",
            f"Run `{self.run_id}`, model `{self.model}`. Prices: `rfq/config.py` PRICES (USD per 1M tokens).", "",
            "| | value |", "|---|---|",
            f"| emails | {len(rows)} ({len(rows) - len(modelled)} skipped: duplicates) |",
            f"| model calls sent this run | {tot['live_calls']} |",
            f"| answers from cache | {hits} |",
            f"| emails with no model answer | {errors} |",
            f"| input tokens (of which cached by provider) | {tot['input_tokens']:,} ({tot['cached_input_tokens']:,}) |",
            f"| output tokens | {tot['output_tokens']:,} |",
            f"| **cost to produce these answers** | **${tot['cost_usd']:.4f}** |",
            f"| cost paid by this run | ${tot['live_cost_usd']:.4f} |",
            f"| per modelled email: calls / tokens / $ | {sum(1 for r in modelled if r.get('cache_hit') or r.get('live_calls'))/n:.2f} / "
            f"{(tot['input_tokens'] + tot['output_tokens'])/n:,.0f} / ${tot['cost_usd']/n:.4f} |",
            "", "Cost to produce = what the original call cost, also for answers now replayed from cache.", "",
            "| email | from cache | calls | in | cached in | out | $ | latency s | images | note |",
            "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
        ]
        for r in rows:
            note = r.get("skipped") or (r.get("error") or "")[:80]
            out.append(
                f"| {r['email']} | {'yes' if r.get('cache_hit') else ''} | {r.get('live_calls', 0)} | "
                f"{r.get('input_tokens', 0):,} | {r.get('cached_input_tokens', 0):,} | {r.get('output_tokens', 0):,} | "
                f"{r.get('cost_usd', 0):.4f} | {r.get('latency_s', 0)} | {r.get('images', 0)} | {note} |"
            )
        return "\n".join(out) + "\n"

content.text:
Step 6 is built and tested, but I haven't run it against the real API. As you asked, here's the cost estimate first.

**Estimated cost for the 24 dev emails:** 23 model calls, because the duplicate E008 is skipped.

| model | input tokens | output tokens | estimated cost | per email |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **gpt-4.1** (current default) | ~46k | ~24k | **~$0.29** | ~$0.012 |
| gpt-4.1-mini | ~50k | ~24k | ~$0.06 | ~$0.003 |

- Output is most of the cost. The two long lists (E006's 42-line RFQ PDF and E021's 50-line BOM) are about a quarter of it.
- Allow ±50%: tokens are counted roughly (about 3.5 characters per token), and output is estimated at 70 tokens per likely item line.
- A repair retry would add one more call for that email.
- The prices are the list prices I know, set in `rfq/config.py`. Check them against OpenAI's pricing page before relying on the dollar figures. The real run will log actual token counts in `reports/cost.md`.

**My recommendation is gpt-4.1.** Even at about $0.29 here, or about $0.50 for the 40 held-out emails, it uses a tiny share of the $20 limit. It should also read the phone photo (E007) and the scan (E009) more reliably than mini, but I haven't measured that.

**What step 6 does:**
- **One call per email**, with structured output and temperature 0. Photos, scanned pages and pasted screenshots go in as images.
- **A schema workaround:** Pydantic's discriminated union produces a schema format I believe OpenAI's strict mode rejects. So the model is sent a plain-union version of the same schema, and its reply is checked against the real discriminated union.
- **The model points, code copies:** for text and table lines, the model gives a row ID. Code copies `raw` from the real line, and `qty`/`uom` from the table cells under a Qty/UOM heading. Code keeps the model's `raw` only when it is a real fragment of the line (one sentence holding several items). For images, the model's own reading is used.
- **Lines code drops:** made-up row IDs, struck rows, rows from a superseded sheet, and quoted-history rows unless the email is a `rfq_revision` or `purchase_order`.
- **Workbooks with several sheets:** if the sheets are versions, only the newest is used; if it's unclear, the email is flagged for review.
- **Cache:** saved responses are keyed on the model, prompt version, schema and email content. Only answers that pass the schema are saved.
- **Retries:** only on rate limits, server errors and timeouts. One repair attempt on a bad answer.
- **No key and nothing cached:** the email is flagged for review. It never crashes.
- **Logs:** `runs/<id>/calls.jsonl`, `failures.jsonl` (with a `retryable` flag), `runs/latest/` and `reports/cost.md`.
- **The key** is only read by the OpenAI client from the environment. A test checks it never appears in any cache or log file.
- **New commands:** `rfq estimate --emails <dir>` prices a run without calling the model, and `rfq parse --offline` uses the cache only.

**Checks so far:**
- All 78 tests pass. The model tests use a fake client, and a test setup file keeps the test suite away from the real API, cache and reports.
- An offline run on dev made 0 calls and 0 crashes: 23 emails came back flagged, plus the duplicate E008. The output passes the format check.
- I fixed one bug the tests caught: two runs in the same second used to share one log folder.

`parsed.json`, `runs/latest/` and `reports/cost.md` currently hold that offline run, and the real run will replace them.

Stopping here. Tell me which model to use and I'll do the first real run.

content.text:
The first real run went badly: almost every request came back with no lines, and it cost $0.62 against my ~$0.29 estimate. Both come from a flaw in the answer schema I designed in step 6. I haven't fixed anything.

**Headline numbers** (`eval --baseline`, 27 changes vs. the stub baseline)

| metric | stub | first real run |
|---|---|---|
| silent losses | 19 | **15** |
| hallucinated lines | 0 | 0 |
| lost requests | 20 | **16** |
| phantom requests | 0 | 0 |
| classification | 1/24 | 7/24 |
| line recall | 0/210 | **0/210** |
| links | 1/2 | 1/2 |
| needs_review precision / recall | n/a / 0/2 | 0/4 / 0/2 |

The 7 correct classifications are mostly the easy non-requests (bounce, newsletter, vendor quote, status inquiry).

**Worst 5 problems**

1. **The schema makes the model choose the type before it reads the email.** This causes 15 silent losses and 16 lost requests.
   - With strict output the model writes the fields in schema order. The no-items shape starts with `kind`, while the three request shapes start with `lines`.
   - Once the model writes `"kind"` first, it's locked into the no-items shape, where `vendor_quote` is the closest choice. 15 customer requests came back as `vendor_quote`.
   - The rationales show the model knows better: E001 says "This is a request for quote (rfq) from a customer… not a quote from a vendor", but is labelled `vendor_quote`.
   - E016, E024 and E007 write "correction: the classification is rfq". E016 even put a whole correct answer, all 6 lines, inside the rationale text.
2. **The four emails that did take a request shape ran away.** E003, E004, E005 and E019 each hit the 16,000-token output limit after about 70 seconds and were rejected.
   - They're short lists (8–20 items), so it's a loop, not real output.
   - Those 4 calls cost **$0.52, 84% of the run**.
   - The rejected output isn't saved anywhere, so I can't see what it looped on.
3. **Purchase orders read as status inquiries.** E015 ("please process the attached PO") and E020 ("go ahead with items 1, 2 and 4") came back `status_inquiry`. E020's rationale says "this is a purchase order". It's the same cause as #1.
4. **Missing or unreadable attachments get no flag.** E017 (BOM not attached) and E022 (password-protected PDF) were both called `vendor_quote`.
   - The no-items shape can't set needs_review, and code ignores read problems on non-request types by design.
   - So both are silent losses, and needs_review recall is 0/2.
5. **Code doesn't question a no-items answer.** When the model says `vendor_quote`, code accepts it, even for a customer's email to our RFQ inbox whose rationale says "rfq". There's no check between the label and the evidence, so the silent-loss guard never fires for these.

**Actual cost** (`reports/cost.md`)

| | |
|---|---|
| model calls | 23 (E008 skipped as a duplicate) |
| input tokens | 71,867 (35,072 served from OpenAI's prompt cache) |
| output tokens | 66,099, of which 64,000 came from the 4 runaway calls |
| **total** | **$0.6199** (vs. ~$0.29 estimated) |
| without the 4 runaways | ~$0.10 for 19 calls, about $0.005 each, because those answers were nearly empty |

Two side notes:
- The 4 rejected answers weren't cached, which is correct. But re-running now would pay for those 4 again, so I won't re-run until the schema is fixed.
- 14 of the 19 non-runaway answers are wrong but now cached. The fix will need a new prompt version so those wrong answers aren't reused.

Stopping. The obvious first fix is to put the reasoning and the type first in every shape, so the model reads before it commits. Plus saving rejected output and lowering the output cap. Say if you want me to go ahead.

Send the model ONE flat schema, in this field order: reasoning (short, max ~3 sentences: who is writing to whom and what they want), classification (enum), needs_review, review_reason, line_items. Code validates afterwards: a non-request type with lines → drop the lines and log it; a request type with no lines and no review flag → needs_review.
Let the model set needs_review for any type, but code keeps it only for request types. Tell the prompt: a customer email pointing at an attachment that’s missing or unreadable is still an rfq with needs_review.

input.content:
"""What the model must return: ONE flat object, fields in the order the model should think.

Strict structured outputs generate fields in schema order, so order is behaviour:
  reasoning      first: who is writing to whom and what they want (before any label)
  classification then the label, informed by the reasoning
  needs_review / review_reason
  sheet_decisions  which sheets of a multi-sheet workbook count, before listing lines
  line_items     last, capped in length (runaway protection)

The model never types `raw` for text/table lines — it points at a row id and code copies the
real text (and qty/uom from table cells). Only lines read from an image carry model-written raw.
Code enforces the rules afterwards (rfq/validate.py): lines on a non-request are dropped,
needs_review is kept only for request types, a request with no lines gets needs_review.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from rfq.config import MAX_LINE_ITEMS

Uom = Literal["EA", "FT", "M", "IN", "BX", "PK", "PR", "DZ", "RL", "LB", "SET", "GAL", "BAG", "CS"]
Classification = Literal[
    "rfq", "rfq_revision", "purchase_order", "vendor_quote", "status_inquiry", "auto_reply", "other"
]


class _Strict(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


class LineOut(_Strict):
    row_id: str | None = Field(
        description="The [row id] of the text/table line this item is on. null only for items read from an image."
    )
    image: str | None = Field(
        description="For items read from an image: the image label exactly as given. Otherwise null."
    )
    raw: str = Field(
        description="The item's text as written. For a row id: the part of that line that is this item "
        "(the whole line if it holds one item). For an image: your transcription of that line."
    )
    description: str = Field(
        description="The item self-contained: its own words plus every heading, note, column header, "
        "sheet name, form field or subject line that applies to it, and nothing that does not."
    )
    qty: float | None = Field(description="Quantity as stated; null if vague ('a couple') or missing.")
    uom: Uom | None = Field(description="Unit as stated, mapped to the allowed list; null if none stated.")


class SheetDecision(_Strict):
    file: str = Field(description="Workbook filename.")
    relation: Literal["sections", "versions", "unclear"] = Field(
        description="sections = parts of one order (use all); versions = revisions of one list "
        "(use only the newest); unclear = cannot tell."
    )
    sheets_used: list[str] = Field(description="Sheet names the lines were taken from.")
    why: str = Field(description="One short sentence: the evidence (sheet names, dates, file name, email text).")


class Extraction(_Strict):
    reasoning: str = Field(
        description="At most 3 short sentences: who is writing to whom, and what they want. "
        "Do not list items here."
    )
    classification: Classification
    needs_review: bool = Field(
        description="true if something asked for cannot be fully read or resolved from this email."
    )
    review_reason: str | None = Field(description="Why, when needs_review is true; else null.")
    sheet_decisions: list[SheetDecision] = Field(
        description="One entry per workbook with 2+ visible sheets. Empty list otherwise."
    )
    line_items: list[LineOut] = Field(
        max_length=MAX_LINE_ITEMS,
        description="The items being asked for. Empty for vendor_quote, status_inquiry, auto_reply, other.",
    )


def response_format() -> dict:
    from openai.lib._pydantic import to_strict_json_schema

    return {
        "type": "json_schema",
        "json_schema": {"name": "extraction", "strict": True, "schema": to_strict_json_schema(Extraction)},

    )

        description="For items read from an image: the image label exactly as given. Otherwise null."
    )
    raw: str = Field(
        description="The item's text as written. For a row id: the part of that line that is this item "
        "(the whole line if it holds one item). For an image: your transcription of that line."
    )
    description: str = Field(
        description="The item self-contained: its own words plus every heading, note, column header, "
        "sheet name, form field or subject line that applies to it, and nothing that does not."
    )
    qty: float | None = Field(description="Quantity as stated; null if vague ('a couple') or missing.")

    file: str = Field(description="Workbook filename.")
    relation: Literal["sections", "versions", "unclear"] = Field(
        description="sections = parts of one order (use all); versions = revisions of one list "
        "(use only the newest); unclear = cannot tell."
    )
    sheets_used: list[str] = Field(description="Sheet names the lines were taken from.")
    why: str = Field(description="One short sentence: the evidence (sheet names, dates, file name, email text).")


class _Request(_Strict):
    lines: list[LineOut]
    sheet_decisions: list[SheetDecision] = Field(
        description="One entry per workbook with 2+ visible sheets. Empty list otherwise."
    )
    needs_review: bool = Field(
        description="true if something asked for cannot be fully read or resolved from this email."
    )
    review_reason: str | None = Field(description="Why, when needs_review is true; else null.")

"""Prompt: fixed instructions + one rendered email (text with row ids, then images).

The system text is identical for every email (so the provider's prompt cache can reuse it) and
holds the rules from data/README.md in general terms — never strings from the dev inbox.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import hashlib

from rfq.config import IMAGE_DETAIL, MAX_PROMPT_CHARS
from rfq.models import Doc, Email

SYSTEM = """\
You read one email from the RFQ inbox of Ridgeline Industrial Supply, a distributor of pipe, \
fittings, flanges, valves, gaskets, bolting and related industrial supplies. Our inbox is \
rfq@ridgeline-supply.example. Anyone at @ridgeline-supply.example is one of our own reps. \
Our quotes are numbered Q-26-...; customers' RFQ and PO numbers are their own.

Decide what the CURRENT message does, and list exactly the items being asked for.

## Classification (kind) — what the current message does, not the subject or the quoted history
- rfq: asks us to price or check availability of items.
- rfq_revision: changes a request made earlier in the same thread (quantities, additions, removals).
- purchase_order: commits to buy — a PO, "please process", "go ahead with items 1-3".
- vendor_quote: a supplier quoting or answering US (e.g. replying to one of our reps' requests), \
however much it looks like a list of items.
- status_inquiry: asks about an existing quote or order (update? ETA? tracking?).
- auto_reply: machine-generated — out-of-office, bounce / delivery failure, read receipt.
- other: marketing, newsletters, invoices, remittances, job applications, internal chatter, \
"we went with someone else".
When one of our reps forwards a customer's email, classify it as the customer's email and also \
read the rep's own note.

## How the email is shown
Every text line has a row id in brackets, e.g. [body!B3] or [file.xlsx!Sheet!R7]. Sections:
- CURRENT MESSAGE (body!B..): the message being classified.
- FORWARDED (body!F..): content forwarded inside this message. It counts as the request when \
our rep forwards a customer's email.
- QUOTED HISTORY (body!Q..): earlier messages. CONTEXT ONLY: they were handled when they arrived. \
Take lines from it only (a) for rfq_revision, to give the complete order as now intended, and \
(b) for purchase_order, when the current message commits to items listed there \
("go ahead with items 1, 2 and 4" -> exactly those items).
- ATTACHMENT sections: spreadsheets (one line per row, cells joined by " | "), PDFs, Word \
documents, CSVs, attached emails. Notes under a heading tell you about hidden sheets, merged \
cells, comments and anything that could not be read.
- IMAGE parts: photos, scans and pasted screenshots. Read them carefully.
Lines marked STRUCK are crossed out: never return them. Lines marked (Heading ...) are headings.

## Line items — one per thing the customer is asking for
- Text or table line: set row_id to that line's id, image to null. raw = the part of the line \
that is this item (the whole line when it holds one item; the fragment when one line holds several).
- Image: set row_id to null, image to the image label exactly as given, raw = your reading of \
that line.
- Not items: headings, notes, column headers, totals, prices, signatures, addresses, crossed-out \
lines, old revisions of a document, items in quoted history (except the two cases above).
- description: the item self-contained, as a rep would type it into a quote without re-reading \
the email: the line's own words plus EVERY heading, note, column header, sheet name, form field, \
subject line or earlier line that applies to it (e.g. a section heading "ALL PIPE SCH 40" applies \
to the rows under it; a document field "Material: X" applies to every row). Do not add context \
that belongs to a different section, and do not carry a default onto a line that overrides it \
("SCH 80" on the line beats "SCH 40 unless noted"). Never invent a spec the email doesn't give.
- qty: the number as the customer stated it, not converted. A spelled-out number is a number. \
A vague amount ("a couple", "some", "enough for the job") is null. A size, schedule, length, \
pressure class, rating, part number or price is NEVER a quantity.
- uom: one of EA FT M IN BX PK PR DZ RL LB SET GAL BAG CS as stated (joints/lengths/pieces/each \
-> EA, feet -> FT, rolls -> RL, pairs -> PR, boxes -> BX, packs -> PK), or null when no unit is stated.
- rfq_revision: return the COMPLETE order as the customer now intends it — unchanged earlier \
items (from quoted history) plus changes, minus removals; a changed line uses its new quantity.

## Several visible sheets in one workbook
Decide for each such workbook, and record it in sheet_decisions:
- sections: the sheets are parts of one order (e.g. pipe on one tab, fittings on another) -> use all.
- versions: the sheets are revisions of the same list -> use only the newest, judged by sheet \
names (Rev B > Rev A, "final", "current", "old"), dates, the file name, or what the email says.
- unclear: you cannot tell -> still return your best lines, and set needs_review with the reason.
Apply the same judgement to several attachments that are versions of one list.

## needs_review — only for rfq, rfq_revision, purchase_order
true when the email asks for something you cannot fully read or resolve: the attachment it points \
at is missing or cannot be opened, part of it could not be read, or items are identified only by \
something not in the email ("same as last time", "same as the one in the photo" when the photo does \
not show what is needed). Give the reason, and still return every line you could read.
"""


def _section(title: str) -> str:
    return f"\n=== {title} ===\n"


def _line_text(ln) -> str:
    tags = []
    if ln.style:
        tags.append(f"({ln.style})")
    if ln.struck:
        tags.append("STRUCK")
    if ln.note:
        tags.append(f"[{ln.note}]")
    return f"[{ln.row_id}] {ln.text}" + (" " + " ".join(tags) if tags else "")


def render_text(email: Email, docs: list[Doc]) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """Render headers + all docs as text. Returns (text, truncated_by_budget)."""
    h = email.headers
    out = [
        f"From: {h.get('from')}" + ("   [one of our reps]" if email.internal else ""),
        f"To: {h.get('to')}",
    ]
    if h.get("cc"):
        out.append(f"Cc: {h.get('cc')}")
    out += [f"Date: {h.get('date')}", f"Subject: {h.get('subject')}"]

    body = docs[0]
    groups = {"B": "CURRENT MESSAGE", "F": "FORWARDED", "Q": "QUOTED HISTORY (context only)"}
    for prefix, title in groups.items():
        lines = [ln for ln in body.lines if ln.row_id.startswith(f"body!{prefix}")]
        if lines:
            out.append(_section(title))
            out += [_line_text(ln) for ln in lines]
    if not any(ln.row_id.startswith("body!B") for ln in body.lines):
        out.append(_section("CURRENT MESSAGE"))
        out.append("(no text)")
    for n in body.notes:
        out.append(f"note: {n}")

    for d in docs[1:]:
        head = f"ATTACHMENT: {d.source} ({d.kind})"
        if d.error:
            head += " — COULD NOT BE READ"
        out.append(_section(head))
        if d.error:
            out.append(f"error: {d.error}")
        for n in d.notes:
            out.append(f"note: {n}")
        for im in d.images:
            out.append(f"(image part follows below, label: {im.label})")
        out += [_line_text(ln) for ln in d.lines]

    text = "\n".join(out)
    if len(text) > MAX_PROMPT_CHARS:
        cut = text[:MAX_PROMPT_CHARS]
        return cut + "\n\n[... email truncated: too long to read in full ...]", True
    return text, False


def build_messages(email: Email, docs: list[Doc]) -> tuple[list[dict], bool]:
    """Chat messages for the model, and whether the text was truncated by the budget."""
    text, truncated = render_text(email, docs)
    content: list[dict] = [{"type": "text", "text": text}]
    for d in docs:
        for im in d.images:
            content.append({"type": "text", "text": f"IMAGE label: {im.label}"})
            b64 = base64.b64encode(im.png).decode("ascii")
            content.append({"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{b64}", "detail": IMAGE_DETAIL}})
    return [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": content}], truncated


def messages_fingerprint(messages: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Stable digest of the request content (images hashed, not inlined)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for m in messages:
        h.update(m["role"].encode())
        content = m["content"]
        parts = [{"type": "text", "text": content}] if isinstance(content, str) else content
        for p in parts:
            if p["type"] == "text":
                h.update(b"T" + p["text"].encode("utf-8"))
            else:
                h.update(b"I" + hashlib.sha256(p["image_url"]["url"].encode()).digest())
                h.update(p["image_url"].get("detail", "").encode())
    return h.hexdigest()

answering one of our reps? a machine?) and what they want. Do not list items here.
2. classification: follows from the reasoning.
3. needs_review / review_reason.

asking for prices is an rfq — even when the list is in an attachment, a photo, or a pasted table, \
and even when that attachment is missing or cannot be opened (then rfq with needs_review).

- purchase_order: commits to buy — a PO, "please process", "go ahead with items 1-3".
- vendor_quote: a SUPPLIER quoting or answering US — typically replying to a request one of \
our reps sent them, with their prices and lead times. However much it looks like a list of items. \

"we went with someone else".

read the rep's own note.

Every text line has a row id in brackets, e.g. [body!B3] or [file.xlsx!Sheet!R7]. Sections:
- CURRENT MESSAGE (body!B..): the message being classified.

our rep forwards a customer's email.
- QUOTED HISTORY (body!Q..): earlier messages. CONTEXT ONLY: they were handled when they arrived. \

documents, CSVs, attached emails. Notes under a heading tell you about hidden sheets, merged \
cells, comments and anything that could not be read.

that line.

pressure class, rating, part number or price is NEVER a quantity.

items (from quoted history) plus changes, minus removals; a changed line uses its new quantity.

Decide for each such workbook, and record it in sheet_decisions:
- sections: the sheets are parts of one order (e.g. pipe on one tab, fittings on another) -> use all.
- versions: the sheets are revisions of the same list -> use only the newest, judged by sheet \
names (Rev B > Rev A, "final", "current", "old"), dates, the file name, or what the email says.
- unclear: you cannot tell -> still return your best lines, and set needs_review with the reason.

    return f"\n=== {title} ===\n"

        tags.append("STRUCK")
    if ln.note:
        tags.append(f"[{ln.note}]")

    """Render headers + all docs as text. Returns (text, truncated_by_budget)."""
    h = email.headers
    out = [
        f"From: {h.get('from')}" + ("   [one of our reps]" if email.internal else ""),
        f"To: {h.get('to')}",
    ]
    if h.get("cc"):
        out.append(f"Cc: {h.get('cc')}")
    out += [f"Date: {h.get('date')}", f"Subject: {h.get('subject')}"]

    body = docs[0]
    groups = {"B": "CURRENT MESSAGE", "F": "FORWARDED", "Q": "QUOTED HISTORY (context only)"}
    for prefix, title in groups.items():
        lines = [ln for ln in body.lines if ln.row_id.startswith(f"body!{prefix}")]
        if lines:
            out.append(_section(title))
            out += [_line_text(ln) for ln in lines]
    if not any(ln.row_id.startswith("body!B") for ln in body.lines):
        out.append(_section("CURRENT MESSAGE"))
        out.append("(no text)")

        out.append(f"note: {n}")

        head = f"ATTACHMENT: {d.source} ({d.kind})"
        if d.error:
            head += " — COULD NOT BE READ"
        out.append(_section(head))
        if d.error:
            out.append(f"error: {d.error}")
        for n in d.notes:
            out.append(f"note: {n}")
        for im in d.images:
            out.append(f"(image part follows below, label: {im.label})")
        out += [_line_text(ln) for ln in d.lines]

    text = "\n".join(out)
    if len(text) > MAX_PROMPT_CHARS:
        cut = text[:MAX_PROMPT_CHARS]
        return cut + "\n\n[... email truncated: too long to read in full ...]", True
    return text, False


def build_messages(email: Email, docs: list[Doc]) -> tuple[list[dict], bool]:
    """Chat messages for the model, and whether the text was truncated by the budget."""
    text, truncated = render_text(email, docs)
    content: list[dict] = [{"type": "text", "text": text}]
    for d in docs:
        for im in d.images:
            content.append({"type": "text", "text": f"IMAGE label: {im.label}"})
            b64 = base64.b64encode(im.png).decode("ascii")
            content.append({"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{b64}", "detail": IMAGE_DETAIL}})
    return [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": content}], truncated


def messages_fingerprint(messages: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Stable digest of the request content (images hashed, not inlined)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for m in messages:
        h.update(m["role"].encode())
        content = m["content"]
        parts = [{"type": "text", "text": content}] if isinstance(content, str) else content
        for p in parts:
            if p["type"] == "text":
                h.update(b"T" + p["text"].encode("utf-8"))
            else:
                h.update(b"I" + hashlib.sha256(p["image_url"]["url"].encode()).digest())
                h.update(p["image_url"].get("detail", "").encode())
    return h.hexdigest()

        return cut + "\n\n[... email truncated: too long to read in full ...]", True
    return text, False


def build_messages(email: Email, docs: list[Doc]) -> tuple[list[dict], bool]:
    """Chat messages for the model, and whether the text was truncated by the budget."""
    text, truncated = render_text(email, docs)
    content: list[dict] = [{"type": "text", "text": text}]
    for d in docs:
        for im in d.images:
            content.append({"type": "text", "text": f"IMAGE label: {im.label}"})
            b64 = base64.b64encode(im.png).decode("ascii")
            content.append({"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{b64}", "detail": IMAGE_DETAIL}})
    return [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": content}], truncated


def messages_fingerprint(messages: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Stable digest of the request content (images hashed, not inlined)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for m in messages:
        h.update(m["role"].encode())
        content = m["content"]
        parts = [{"type": "text", "text": content}] if isinstance(content, str) else content
        for p in parts:
            if p["type"] == "text":
                h.update(b"T" + p["text"].encode("utf-8"))
            else:
                h.update(b"I" + hashlib.sha256(p["image_url"]["url"].encode()).digest())
                h.update(p["image_url"].get("detail", "").encode())
    return h.hexdigest()

"""One structured-output call per email, behind the cache.

Order: cache hit -> done (no network). Miss + no key / offline -> error outcome (flagged
upstream, never a crash). Miss + key -> call with retries on transient errors only
(429, 5xx, timeout, connection), validate against the schema, one repair turn if invalid,
cache only a valid result.

The API key is read by the OpenAI client from the environment. It is never logged or stored.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from pydantic import ValidationError
from tenacity import Retrying, retry_if_exception, stop_after_attempt, wait_exponential

from rfq.cache import Cache, cache_key
from rfq.config import (MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, MAX_RETRIES, MODEL, PRICES, PROMPT_VERSION,
                        REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S, TEMPERATURE, api_key_present)
from rfq.models import Doc, Email
from rfq.prompt import build_messages, messages_fingerprint
from rfq.schema import Extraction, response_format


@dataclass
class Usage:
    input_tokens: int = 0
    cached_input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0

    def add(self, other: "Usage") -> None:
        self.input_tokens += other.input_tokens
        self.cached_input_tokens += other.cached_input_tokens
        self.output_tokens += other.output_tokens


def cost_usd(model: str, u: Usage) -> float:
    p_in, p_cached, p_out = PRICES.get(model, (0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    fresh = max(0, u.input_tokens - u.cached_input_tokens)
    return (fresh * p_in + u.cached_input_tokens * p_cached + u.output_tokens * p_out) / 1e6


@dataclass
class Outcome:
    extraction: Extraction | None
    key: str
    cache_hit: bool = False
    live_calls: int = 0  # HTTP requests actually sent this run
    usage: Usage = field(default_factory=Usage)  # tokens of the call that produced the answer
    cost_usd: float = 0.0  # what producing the answer cost (also reported for cache hits)
    live_cost_usd: float = 0.0  # what THIS run paid (0 on a cache hit)
    latency_s: float = 0.0
    error: str | None = None
    retryable: bool = False
    prompt_truncated: bool = False


def _transient(e: BaseException) -> bool:
    import openai

    if isinstance(e, (openai.RateLimitError, openai.APITimeoutError, openai.APIConnectionError,
                      openai.InternalServerError)):
        return True
    return isinstance(e, openai.APIStatusError) and getattr(e, "status_code", 0) >= 500


def _usage(resp) -> Usage:
    u = getattr(resp, "usage", None)
    if u is None:
        return Usage()
    details = getattr(u, "prompt_tokens_details", None)
    return Usage(
        input_tokens=int(getattr(u, "prompt_tokens", 0) or 0),
        cached_input_tokens=int(getattr(details, "cached_tokens", 0) or 0) if details else 0,
        output_tokens=int(getattr(u, "completion_tokens", 0) or 0),
    )


def offline() -> bool:
    return os.environ.get("RFQ_OFFLINE", "").strip() not in ("", "0", "false")


class Extractor:
    def __init__(self, model: str = MODEL, cache: Cache | None = None, client=None,
                 wait_max_s: float = 20.0) -> None:
        self.model = model
        self.cache = cache or Cache()
        self._client = client
        self._schema = response_format()
        self._wait_max = wait_max_s

    def _get_client(self):
        if self._client is not None:
            return self._client
        if offline() or not api_key_present():
            return None
        from openai import OpenAI

        self._client = OpenAI(timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S, max_retries=0)  # we retry ourselves
        return self._client

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ public
    def run(self, email: Email, docs: list[Doc]) -> Outcome:
        messages, truncated = build_messages(email, docs)
        key = cache_key(self.model, PROMPT_VERSION, self._schema, messages_fingerprint(messages))
        out = Outcome(extraction=None, key=key, prompt_truncated=truncated)

        hit = self.cache.get(key)
        if hit is not None:
            try:
                out.extraction = Extraction.model_validate(hit["response"])
                out.cache_hit = True
                out.usage = Usage(**hit.get("usage", {}))
                out.cost_usd = float(hit.get("cost_usd", 0.0))
                return out
            except (ValidationError, KeyError, TypeError):
                pass  # stale/corrupt entry: treat as a miss

        client = self._get_client()
        if client is None:
            out.error = "model unavailable (no API key or offline) and no cached response"
            out.retryable = True
            return out

        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            self._call_and_validate(client, messages, out)
        except Exception as e:  # anything unexpected: flagged, never a crash
            out.error = f"model call failed: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:300]}"
            out.retryable = _transient(e) or _auth_or_quota(e)
        out.latency_s = round(time.monotonic() - t0, 2)
        out.cost_usd = out.live_cost_usd = round(cost_usd(self.model, out.usage), 6)

        if out.extraction is not None:
            self.cache.put(key, {
                "key": key,
                "email_id": email.id,
                "model": self.model,
                "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
                "created": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
                "usage": out.usage.__dict__,
                "cost_usd": out.cost_usd,
                "response": out.extraction.model_dump(mode="json"),
            })
        return out

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ internals
    def _send(self, client, messages: list[dict], out: Outcome):
        retrying = Retrying(
            retry=retry_if_exception(_transient),
            stop=stop_after_attempt(MAX_RETRIES + 1),
            wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=1, max=self._wait_max),
            reraise=True,
        )
        for attempt in retrying:
            with attempt:
                out.live_calls += 1
                resp = client.chat.completions.create(
                    model=self.model,
                    messages=messages,
                    response_format=self._schema,
                    temperature=TEMPERATURE,
                    max_completion_tokens=MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS,
                )
                out.usage.add(_usage(resp))
                return resp
        raise RuntimeError("unreachable")

    def _call_and_validate(self, client, messages: list[dict], out: Outcome) -> None:
        resp = self._send(client, messages, out)
        problem, extraction, content = _check(resp)
        if extraction is None and problem and problem.startswith("invalid"):
            repair = messages + [
                {"role": "assistant", "content": content or ""},
                {"role": "user", "content": f"That output was {problem}. Return the corrected JSON only."},
            ]
            resp = self._send(client, repair, out)
            problem, extraction, _ = _check(resp)
        out.extraction = extraction
        if extraction is None:
            out.error = f"model output rejected: {problem}"
            out.retryable = False


def _auth_or_quota(e: BaseException) -> bool:
    import openai

    return isinstance(e, (openai.AuthenticationError, openai.PermissionDeniedError))


def _check(resp) -> tuple[str | None, Extraction | None, str | None]:
    """(problem, extraction, raw content). problem starts with 'invalid' when a repair may help."""
    choice = resp.choices[0]
    msg = choice.message
    if getattr(msg, "refusal", None):
        return f"refused: {msg.refusal}", None, None
    if choice.finish_reason == "length":
        return "too long (hit the output token limit)", None, msg.content
    content = msg.content or ""
    try:
        return None, Extraction.model_validate(json.loads(content)), content
    except (ValueError, ValidationError) as e:
        return f"invalid: {str(e)[:400]}", None, content

"""Per-run logs and the cost report.

runs/<run_id>/calls.jsonl     one line per email: cache hit?, tokens, $, latency, error
runs/<run_id>/failures.jsonl  emails that could not get a model answer, with `retryable`
runs/latest/                  copy of the most recent run (committed)
reports/cost.md               totals and per-email table
Never contains the API key or request content.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import secrets
import shutil
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.config import REPORTS_DIR, RUNS_DIR


class RunLog:
    def __init__(self, model: str, runs_dir: Path = RUNS_DIR, reports_dir: Path = REPORTS_DIR) -> None:
        self.model = model
        # timestamp for humans + random suffix so two runs in the same second never share a folder
        self.run_id = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ") + "-" + secrets.token_hex(3)
        self.dir = runs_dir / self.run_id
        self.dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        self.runs_dir = runs_dir
        self.reports_dir = reports_dir
        self.rows: list[dict] = []

    def _append(self, name: str, row: dict) -> None:
        with (self.dir / name).open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

    def record(self, email_id: str, outcome=None, *, skipped: str | None = None, n_images: int = 0) -> None:
        if outcome is None:
            row = {"email": email_id, "skipped": skipped, "live_calls": 0, "cache_hit": False,
                   "input_tokens": 0, "cached_input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0,
                   "cost_usd": 0.0, "live_cost_usd": 0.0, "latency_s": 0.0, "images": 0, "error": None}
        else:
            row = {
                "email": email_id, "skipped": None, "model": self.model,
                "cache_hit": outcome.cache_hit, "live_calls": outcome.live_calls,
                "input_tokens": outcome.usage.input_tokens,
                "cached_input_tokens": outcome.usage.cached_input_tokens,
                "output_tokens": outcome.usage.output_tokens,
                "cost_usd": outcome.cost_usd, "live_cost_usd": outcome.live_cost_usd,
                "latency_s": outcome.latency_s, "images": n_images,
                "prompt_truncated": outcome.prompt_truncated, "error": outcome.error,
            }
            if outcome.error:
                self._append("failures.jsonl", {"email": email_id, "error": outcome.error,
                                                "retryable": outcome.retryable})
        self.rows.append(row)
        self._append("calls.jsonl", row)

    def finish(self) -> Path:
        report = self.render()
        self.reports_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (self.reports_dir / "cost.md").write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
        (self.dir / "cost.md").write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
        latest = self.runs_dir / "latest"
        if latest.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(latest)
        shutil.copytree(self.dir, latest)
        return self.reports_dir / "cost.md"

    def render(self) -> str:
        rows = self.rows
        modelled = [r for r in rows if not r.get("skipped")]
        tot = {k: sum(r.get(k, 0) or 0 for r in rows) for k in
               ("live_calls", "input_tokens", "cached_input_tokens", "output_tokens", "cost_usd", "live_cost_usd")}
        hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("cache_hit"))
        errors = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("error"))
        n = max(len(modelled), 1)
        out = [
            "# Cost report", "",
            f"Run `{self.run_id}`, model `{self.model}`. Prices: `rfq/config.py` PRICES (USD per 1M tokens).", "",
            "| | value |", "|---|---|",
            f"| emails | {len(rows)} ({len(rows) - len(modelled)} skipped: duplicates) |",
            f"| model calls sent this run | {tot['live_calls']} |",
            f"| answers from cache | {hits} |",
            f"| emails with no model answer | {errors} |",
            f"| input tokens (of which cached by provider) | {tot['input_tokens']:,} ({tot['cached_input_tokens']:,}) |",
            f"| output tokens | {tot['output_tokens']:,} |",
            f"| **cost to produce these answers** | **${tot['cost_usd']:.4f}** |",
            f"| cost paid by this run | ${tot['live_cost_usd']:.4f} |",
            f"| per modelled email: calls / tokens / $ | {sum(1 for r in modelled if r.get('cache_hit') or r.get('live_calls'))/n:.2f} / "
            f"{(tot['input_tokens'] + tot['output_tokens'])/n:,.0f} / ${tot['cost_usd']/n:.4f} |",
            "", "Cost to produce = what the original call cost, also for answers now replayed from cache.", "",
            "| email | from cache | calls | in | cached in | out | $ | latency s | images | note |",
            "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
        ]
        for r in rows:
            note = r.get("skipped") or (r.get("error") or "")[:80]
            out.append(
                f"| {r['email']} | {'yes' if r.get('cache_hit') else ''} | {r.get('live_calls', 0)} | "
                f"{r.get('input_tokens', 0):,} | {r.get('cached_input_tokens', 0):,} | {r.get('output_tokens', 0):,} | "
                f"{r.get('cost_usd', 0):.4f} | {r.get('latency_s', 0)} | {r.get('images', 0)} | {note} |"
            )
        return "\n".join(out) + "\n"

"""Command line: `rfq parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json` (or `python -m rfq parse ...`)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.config import MODEL


def _write_json_atomic(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    tmp.replace(path)


def cmd_parse(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    import os

    from rfq.pipeline import run_inbox

    emails_dir = Path(args.emails)
    if not emails_dir.is_dir():
        print(f"--emails: not a directory: {emails_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if args.offline:
        os.environ["RFQ_OFFLINE"] = "1"
    results, runlog = run_inbox(emails_dir, model=args.model)
    _write_json_atomic(Path(args.out), results)
    rows = runlog.rows
    calls = sum(r.get("live_calls", 0) for r in rows)
    hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("cache_hit"))
    errs = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("error"))
    paid = sum(r.get("live_cost_usd", 0) for r in rows)
    print(f"wrote {len(results)} emails to {args.out} | model calls: {calls}, cache hits: {hits}, "
          f"no answer: {errs}, paid this run: ${paid:.4f} | log: {runlog.dir}")
    return 0


def cmd_estimate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Price a run before making it: render every prompt, count tokens approximately."""
    from rfq.estimate import estimate_email
    from rfq.extractors import extract_all
    from rfq.mime import parse_message
    from rfq.pipeline import link_inbox
    from rfq.prompt import build_messages

    emails = [parse_message(p.read_bytes(), p.stem) for p in sorted(Path(args.emails).glob("*.eml"))]
    dups, _ = link_inbox(emails)
    print(f"model {args.model}; {len(dups)} duplicate(s) skipped\n")
    print(f"{'email':8} {'in tok':>8} {'out tok':>8} {'imgs':>4} {'$':>8}")
    tot_in = tot_out = 0
    tot = 0.0
    for e in emails:
        if e.id in dups:
            continue
        docs = extract_all(e)
        est = estimate_email(e.id, args.model, build_messages(e, docs)[0], docs)
        tot_in += est.input_tokens
        tot_out += est.output_tokens
        tot += est.cost_usd
        print(f"{e.id:8} {est.input_tokens:>8,} {est.output_tokens:>8,} {est.images:>4} {est.cost_usd:>8.4f}")
    print(f"{'TOTAL':8} {tot_in:>8,} {tot_out:>8,} {'':>4} {tot:>8.4f}")
    return 0


def cmd_inspect(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Dump how the MIME layer sees each email (no model calls)."""
    from rfq.extractors import describe_docs, extract_all
    from rfq.mime import describe, parse_message

    target = Path(args.path)
    paths = sorted(target.glob("*.eml")) if target.is_dir() else [target]
    chunks = []
    for p in paths:
        try:
            email = parse_message(p.read_bytes(), p.stem)
            chunks.append(describe(email) + describe_docs(extract_all(email)))
        except Exception as e:
            chunks.append(f"===== {p.stem}\nPARSE ERROR: {type(e).__name__}: {e}\n")
    text = "\n".join(chunks)
    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"wrote {len(paths)} emails to {args.out}")
    else:
        print(text)
    return 0


def cmd_links(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Show duplicate and thread links found in code (no model calls)."""
    from rfq.mime import parse_message
    from rfq.pipeline import link_inbox

    emails = []
    for p in sorted(Path(args.emails).glob("*.eml")):
        try:
            emails.append(parse_message(p.read_bytes(), p.stem))
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"{p.stem}: PARSE ERROR {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
    dups, parents = link_inbox(emails)
    for e in emails:
        bits = []
        if e.id in dups:
            bits.append(f"duplicate_of={dups[e.id]}")
        if e.id in parents:
            bits.append(f"thread_parent={parents[e.id]}")
        if bits:
            print(f"{e.id}: {'  '.join(bits)}   [{e.headers.get('subject')}]")
    print(f"{len(dups)} duplicate(s), {len(parents)} thread link(s)")
    return 0


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="rfq", description="Ridgeline RFQ inbox parser")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("parse", help="parse every .eml in a directory")
    p.add_argument("--emails", required=True, help="directory of .eml files")
    p.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output JSON path")
    p.add_argument("--model", default=MODEL, help=f"OpenAI model (default {MODEL})")
    p.add_argument("--offline", action="store_true", help="never call the model; cache only")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_parse)
    es = sub.add_parser("estimate", help="estimate tokens and cost of a run (no model calls)")
    es.add_argument("--emails", required=True, help="directory of .eml files")
    es.add_argument("--model", default=MODEL)
    es.set_defaults(func=cmd_estimate)
    i = sub.add_parser("inspect", help="show how emails are split (no model calls)")
    i.add_argument("path", help=".eml file or directory")
    i.add_argument("--out", help="write to this file instead of stdout")
    i.set_defaults(func=cmd_inspect)
    lk = sub.add_parser("links", help="show duplicate / thread links (no model calls)")
    lk.add_argument("--emails", required=True, help="directory of .eml files")
    lk.set_defaults(func=cmd_links)
    return ap


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
        sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    return args.func(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

            chunks.append(f"===== {p.stem}\nPARSE ERROR: {type(e).__name__}: {e}\n")
    text = "\n".join(chunks)
    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"wrote {len(paths)} emails to {args.out}")
    else:
        print(text)
    return 0


def cmd_links(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Show duplicate and thread links found in code (no model calls)."""
    from rfq.mime import parse_message
    from rfq.pipeline import link_inbox

    emails = []
    for p in sorted(Path(args.emails).glob("*.eml")):
        try:
            emails.append(parse_message(p.read_bytes(), p.stem))
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"{p.stem}: PARSE ERROR {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
    dups, parents = link_inbox(emails)
    for e in emails:
        bits = []
        if e.id in dups:
            bits.append(f"duplicate_of={dups[e.id]}")
        if e.id in parents:
            bits.append(f"thread_parent={parents[e.id]}")
        if bits:
            print(f"{e.id}: {'  '.join(bits)}   [{e.headers.get('subject')}]")
    print(f"{len(dups)} duplicate(s), {len(parents)} thread link(s)")
    return 0


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="rfq", description="Ridgeline RFQ inbox parser")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("parse", help="parse every .eml in a directory")
    p.add_argument("--emails", required=True, help="directory of .eml files")
    p.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output JSON path")
    p.add_argument("--model", default=MODEL, help=f"OpenAI model (default {MODEL})")
    p.add_argument("--offline", action="store_true", help="never call the model; cache only")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_parse)
    es = sub.add_parser("estimate", help="estimate tokens and cost of a run (no model calls)")
    es.add_argument("--emails", required=True, help="directory of .eml files")
    es.add_argument("--model", default=MODEL)
    es.set_defaults(func=cmd_estimate)
    i = sub.add_parser("inspect", help="show how emails are split (no model calls)")
    i.add_argument("path", help=".eml file or directory")
    i.add_argument("--out", help="write to this file instead of stdout")
    i.set_defaults(func=cmd_inspect)
    lk = sub.add_parser("links", help="show duplicate / thread links (no model calls)")
    lk.add_argument("--emails", required=True, help="directory of .eml files")
    lk.set_defaults(func=cmd_links)
    return ap


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
        sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    return args.func(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Model-call tests with a fake OpenAI client (no network, no key)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import openai
import pytest

from rfq.cache import Cache
from rfq.llm import Extractor
from rfq.models import Doc, Email, ImagePart, Line
from rfq.prompt import build_messages
from rfq.schema import response_format

GOOD = {"result": {"kind": "rfq", "lines": [
    {"row_id": "body!B1", "image": None, "raw": "4 ea 2in tee", "description": "2in tee", "qty": 4, "uom": "EA"}],
    "sheet_decisions": [], "needs_review": False, "review_reason": None, "rationale": "asks for prices"}}


def _resp(content: str, finish: str = "stop", refusal=None, tokens=(1000, 200)):
    msg = SimpleNamespace(content=content, refusal=refusal)
    usage = SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=tokens[0], completion_tokens=tokens[1],
                            prompt_tokens_details=SimpleNamespace(cached_tokens=0))
    return SimpleNamespace(choices=[SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason=finish)], usage=usage)


class FakeClient:
    """Replays a script of responses / exceptions; records every request."""

    def __init__(self, script):
        self.script = list(script)
        self.requests: list[dict] = []
        self.chat = SimpleNamespace(completions=SimpleNamespace(create=self._create))

    def _create(self, **kw):
        self.requests.append(kw)
        item = self.script.pop(0)
        if isinstance(item, Exception):
            raise item
        return item


def _email() -> tuple[Email, list[Doc]]:
    e = Email(id="T1", headers={"subject": "RFQ"}, body="4 ea 2in tee")
    return e, [Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[Line("body!B1", "4 ea 2in tee")])]


def _transient() -> Exception:
    req = openai._base_client.httpx.Request("POST", "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions") \
        if hasattr(openai._base_client, "httpx") else None
    return openai.APITimeoutError(request=req)


def _ex(tmp_path: Path, script) -> tuple[Extractor, FakeClient]:
    client = FakeClient(script)
    return Extractor(model="gpt-4.1", cache=Cache(tmp_path / "cache"), client=client, wait_max_s=0.01), client


def test_valid_answer_is_cached_and_second_run_makes_no_call(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, client = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    e, docs = _email()
    first = ex.run(e, docs)
    assert first.extraction and not first.cache_hit and first.live_calls == 1
    assert first.cost_usd == pytest.approx((1000 * 2.0 + 200 * 8.0) / 1e6)
    second = ex.run(e, docs)  # script is empty now: any call would raise IndexError
    assert second.cache_hit and second.live_calls == 0 and second.live_cost_usd == 0
    assert second.cost_usd == first.cost_usd  # cost to produce is still reported
    assert len(client.requests) == 1


def test_request_uses_strict_schema_and_temperature_zero(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, client = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    ex.run(*_email())
    req = client.requests[0]
    assert req["response_format"] == response_format() and req["temperature"] == 0
    assert req["messages"][0]["role"] == "system"


def test_invalid_then_repaired(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, client = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp('{"result": {"kind": "rfq"}}'), _resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction and out.live_calls == 2
    assert "corrected JSON" in client.requests[1]["messages"][-1]["content"]


def test_invalid_twice_is_error_and_not_cached(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp("not json"), _resp("still not json")])
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction is None and "rejected" in out.error and not out.retryable
    assert not list((tmp_path / "cache").glob("*.json")) if (tmp_path / "cache").exists() else True


def test_transient_errors_are_retried(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_transient(), _transient(), _resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction and out.live_calls == 3


def test_transient_errors_exhausted_is_retryable_failure(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_transient()] * 4)
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction is None and out.retryable and out.live_calls == 4


def test_refusal_and_length_are_errors(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp("", refusal="no")])
    assert "refused" in ex.run(*_email()).error
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp('{"result":', finish="length")])
    assert "too long" in ex.run(*_email()).error


def test_no_key_and_cache_miss_is_flagged_not_crash(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex = Extractor(model="gpt-4.1", cache=Cache(tmp_path / "cache"))  # offline via conftest
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction is None and out.retryable and "no cached response" in out.error


def test_cache_key_changes_with_content_model_and_prompt_version(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp(json.dumps(GOOD))] * 3)
    e, docs = _email()
    k1 = ex.run(e, docs).key
    docs2 = [Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[Line("body!B1", "5 ea 2in tee")])]
    assert ex.run(e, docs2).key != k1

def test_images_go_as_vision_parts() -> None:
    e = Email(id="T2", headers={}, body="see photo")
    docs = [Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[Line("body!B1", "see photo")]),
            Doc(source="IMG_1.jpg", kind="image", images=[ImagePart("IMG_1.jpg", b"\x89PNG", 10, 10)])]

    assert any(p["type"] == "text" and p["text"] == "IMAGE label: IMG_1.jpg" for p in parts)


def test_key_is_never_written_to_cache_or_logs(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    from rfq.costlog import RunLog

    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "sk-test-SECRET-123")

"""Model answer -> Result: code owns raw/qty/uom and the drop rules (synthetic data)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from rfq.models import Doc, Email, Line
from rfq.schema import Extraction
from rfq.validate import build_result, normalize_uom


def _ln(row_id, raw, desc="d", qty=None, uom=None, image=None):
    return {"row_id": row_id, "image": image, "raw": raw, "description": desc, "qty": qty, "uom": uom}


def _ans(kind, lines, **kw):
    body = {"kind": kind, "lines": lines, "sheet_decisions": kw.get("sheets", []),
            "needs_review": kw.get("review", False), "review_reason": kw.get("reason"), "rationale": "r"}
    return Extraction.model_validate({"result": body})


EMAIL = Email(id="T", headers={}, body="")
BODY = Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[
    Line("body!B1", "Please quote: 10 of the 1/2 90s and 6 tees same size"),
    Line("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve"),
    Line("body!Q1", "8 ea 3in cap"),
])
SHEET = Doc(source="bom.xlsx", kind="xlsx", lines=[
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R1", "ALL SCH 40", cells=["ALL SCH 40"]),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R2", "Item | Qty | UOM | Size", cells=["Item", "Qty", "UOM", "Size"]),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R3", 'Tee | 12 | EA | 2"', cells=["Tee", "12", "EA", '2"']),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R4", 'Cap | 3 | EA | 2"', cells=["Cap", "3", "EA", '2"'], struck=True),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R5", 'Pipe | 40 ft | | 2"', cells=["Pipe", "40 ft", "", '2"']),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev A!R3", 'Tee | 8 | EA | 2"', cells=["Tee", "8", "EA", '2"']),
])
DOCS = [BODY, SHEET]


def test_table_row_raw_qty_uom_come_from_cells_not_model() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [_ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R3", "tee twelve", qty=99, uom="FT")]))
    li = r.line_items[0]
    assert (li.raw, li.qty, li.uom, li.source) == ('Tee | 12 | EA | 2"', 12, "EA", "bom.xlsx")


def test_unit_inside_qty_cell() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [_ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R5", "pipe")]))
    assert (r.line_items[0].qty, r.line_items[0].uom) == (40, "FT")


def test_fragment_kept_when_grounded_else_whole_line() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [
        _ln("body!B1", "10 of the 1/2 90s", qty=10),
        _ln("body!B1", "6 tees same size", qty=6),
        _ln("body!B2", "four gate valves 2 inch", qty=4, uom="EA"),  # not a fragment of the line
    ]))
    assert [li.raw for li in r.line_items] == ["10 of the 1/2 90s", "6 tees same size", "4 ea 2in gate valve"]


def test_unknown_struck_and_quoted_rows_dropped_for_rfq() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [
        _ln("body!B9", "invented"), _ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R4", "cap"), _ln("body!Q1", "8 ea 3in cap"),
        _ln("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve", qty=4),
    ]))
    assert [li.raw for li in r.line_items] == ["4 ea 2in gate valve"]


def test_quoted_rows_allowed_for_revision_and_po() -> None:
    for kind in ("rfq_revision", "purchase_order"):
        r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans(kind, [_ln("body!Q1", "8 ea 3in cap", qty=8)]), parent="P1")

    return {"row_id": row_id, "image": image, "raw": raw, "description": desc, "qty": qty, "uom": uom}


def _ans(kind, lines, **kw):
    return Extraction.model_validate({

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scanned-row numbering check
_ITEM_NO = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:item\s*)?#?\s*(\d{1,4})\s*(?:[|.):\-]|\s)", re.I)


def numbering_problem(raws: list[str]) -> str | None:
    """Item numbers read from an image should run 1, 2, 3 ... A skip or repeat means a row was
    probably dropped, doubled or read from the wrong line. Only applies when the leading numbers
    really are an item sequence (not, say, quantities at the start of each line). Numbering that
    restarts at 1 (a new section) is fine."""
    nums = [int(m.group(1)) for r in raws if (m := _ITEM_NO.match(r))]
    if len(nums) < 3 or len(nums) < 0.8 * len(raws):
        return None
    steps = [b - a for a, b in zip(nums, nums[1:])]
    if sum(1 for s in steps if s == 1) < 0.6 * len(steps):
        return None  # leading numbers don't form a sequence: not item numbers
    issues: list[str] = []
    segment: list[int] = []
    for n in nums + [1]:  # sentinel restart flushes the last segment
        if segment and n == 1:
            seen = set()
            for a, b in zip(segment, segment[1:]):
                if b == a or b in seen:
                    issues.append(f"{b} repeated")
                elif b > a + 1:
                    issues.append(f"{a + 1}-{b - 1} missing" if b > a + 2 else f"{a + 1} missing")
                elif b < a:
                    issues.append(f"{b} after {a}")
                seen.add(a)
            segment = []
        segment.append(n)
    return ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(issues)) or None
