"""Model answer -> Result: code owns raw/qty/uom and the drop rules (synthetic data)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from rfq.models import Doc, Email, Line
from rfq.schema import Extraction
from rfq.validate import build_result, normalize_uom


def _ln(row_id, raw, desc="d", qty=None, uom=None, image=None):
    return {"row_id": row_id, "image": image, "raw": raw, "description": desc, "qty": qty, "uom": uom}


def _ans(kind, lines, **kw):
    return Extraction.model_validate({
        "reasoning": "r", "classification": kind, "needs_review": kw.get("review", False),
        "review_reason": kw.get("reason"), "sheet_decisions": kw.get("sheets", []), "line_items": lines,
    })


EMAIL = Email(id="T", headers={}, body="")
BODY = Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[
    Line("body!B1", "Please quote: 10 of the 1/2 90s and 6 tees same size"),
    Line("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve"),
    Line("body!Q1", "8 ea 3in cap"),
])
SHEET = Doc(source="bom.xlsx", kind="xlsx", lines=[
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R1", "ALL SCH 40", cells=["ALL SCH 40"]),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R2", "Item | Qty | UOM | Size", cells=["Item", "Qty", "UOM", "Size"]),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R3", 'Tee | 12 | EA | 2"', cells=["Tee", "12", "EA", '2"']),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R4", 'Cap | 3 | EA | 2"', cells=["Cap", "3", "EA", '2"'], struck=True),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R5", 'Pipe | 40 ft | | 2"', cells=["Pipe", "40 ft", "", '2"']),
    Line("bom.xlsx!Rev A!R3", 'Tee | 8 | EA | 2"', cells=["Tee", "8", "EA", '2"']),
])
DOCS = [BODY, SHEET]


def test_table_row_raw_qty_uom_come_from_cells_not_model() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [_ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R3", "tee twelve", qty=99, uom="FT")]))
    li = r.line_items[0]
    assert (li.raw, li.qty, li.uom, li.source) == ('Tee | 12 | EA | 2"', 12, "EA", "bom.xlsx")


def test_unit_inside_qty_cell() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [_ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R5", "pipe")]))
    assert (r.line_items[0].qty, r.line_items[0].uom) == (40, "FT")


def test_fragment_kept_when_grounded_else_whole_line() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [
        _ln("body!B1", "10 of the 1/2 90s", qty=10),
        _ln("body!B1", "6 tees same size", qty=6),
        _ln("body!B2", "four gate valves 2 inch", qty=4, uom="EA"),  # not a fragment of the line
    ]))
    assert [li.raw for li in r.line_items] == ["10 of the 1/2 90s", "6 tees same size", "4 ea 2in gate valve"]


def test_unknown_struck_and_quoted_rows_dropped_for_rfq() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [
        _ln("body!B9", "invented"), _ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R4", "cap"), _ln("body!Q1", "8 ea 3in cap"),
        _ln("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve", qty=4),
    ]))
    assert [li.raw for li in r.line_items] == ["4 ea 2in gate valve"]


def test_quoted_rows_allowed_for_revision_and_po() -> None:
    for kind in ("rfq_revision", "purchase_order"):
        r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans(kind, [_ln("body!Q1", "8 ea 3in cap", qty=8)]), parent="P1")
        assert [li.raw for li in r.line_items] == ["8 ea 3in cap"]
        assert r.revises == ("P1" if kind == "rfq_revision" else None)


def test_versions_keep_only_newest_sheet_and_unclear_flags() -> None:
    lines = [_ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R3", "tee"), _ln("bom.xlsx!Rev A!R3", "tee")]
    sd = {"file": "bom.xlsx", "relation": "versions", "sheets_used": ["Rev B"], "why": "Rev B is newer"}
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", lines, sheets=[sd]))
    assert [li.qty for li in r.line_items] == [12] and not r.needs_review
    sd_unclear = {**sd, "relation": "unclear", "sheets_used": ["Rev B", "Rev A"]}
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", lines, sheets=[sd_unclear]))
    assert r.needs_review and "sections or versions" in r.review_reason and len(r.line_items) == 2


def test_image_lines_keep_model_raw_and_map_source() -> None:
    img = Doc(source="scan.pdf", kind="pdf")
    from rfq.models import ImagePart

    img.images = [ImagePart("scan.pdf page 2", b"x", 1, 1)]
    r = build_result(EMAIL, [BODY, img], _ans("rfq", [_ln(None, "6 - 4in blind flg", qty=6, image="scan.pdf page 2")]))
    assert (r.line_items[0].raw, r.line_items[0].source) == ("6 - 4in blind flg", "scan.pdf")


def test_non_request_lines_and_review_flag_are_dropped(caplog) -> None:
    for kind in ("vendor_quote", "status_inquiry", "auto_reply", "other"):
        ans = _ans(kind, [_ln("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve", qty=4)], review=True, reason="x")
        with caplog.at_level("INFO"):
            r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, ans, problems=["x.pdf: broken"])
        assert r.classification == kind and r.line_items == [] and not r.needs_review and r.review_reason is None
    assert "dropped" in caplog.text


def test_read_problems_force_review_on_a_request() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [_ln("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve", qty=4)]),
                     problems=["rfq.pdf: PDF is password-protected"])
    assert r.needs_review and "password-protected" in r.review_reason and r.line_items


def test_list_at_the_item_cap_is_flagged(monkeypatch) -> None:
    import rfq.validate as v

    monkeypatch.setattr(v, "MAX_LINE_ITEMS", 2)
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [_ln("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve"), _ln("bom.xlsx!Rev B!R3", "tee")]))
    assert r.needs_review and "limit" in r.review_reason


def test_review_reasons_merge_and_silent_loss_guard() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", []))
    assert r.needs_review and "no line items" in r.review_reason
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, _ans("rfq", [_ln("body!B2", "4 ea 2in gate valve")], review=True,
                                       reason="BOM not attached"), problems=["a.pdf: password-protected"])
    assert r.needs_review and "BOM not attached" in r.review_reason and "password" in r.review_reason


def test_no_answer_is_flagged_request() -> None:
    r = build_result(EMAIL, DOCS, None, model_error="model unavailable")
    assert r.classification == "rfq" and r.needs_review and "model unavailable" in r.review_reason

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scanned-row numbering check
_ITEM_NO = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:item\s*)?#?\s*(\d{1,4})\s*(?:[|.):\-]|\s)", re.I)


def numbering_problem(raws: list[str]) -> str | None:
    """Item numbers read from an image should run 1, 2, 3 ... A skip or repeat means a row was
    probably dropped, doubled or read from the wrong line. Only applies when the leading numbers
    really are an item sequence (not, say, quantities at the start of each line). Numbering that
    restarts at 1 (a new section) is fine."""
    nums = [int(m.group(1)) for r in raws if (m := _ITEM_NO.match(r))]
    if len(nums) < 3 or len(nums) < 0.8 * len(raws):
        return None
    steps = [b - a for a, b in zip(nums, nums[1:])]
    if sum(1 for s in steps if s == 1) < 0.6 * len(steps):
        return None  # leading numbers don't form a sequence: not item numbers
    issues: list[str] = []
    segment: list[int] = []
    for n in nums + [1]:  # sentinel restart flushes the last segment
        if segment and n == 1:
            seen = set()
            for a, b in zip(segment, segment[1:]):
                if b == a or b in seen:
                    issues.append(f"{b} repeated")
                elif b > a + 1:
                    issues.append(f"{a + 1}-{b - 1} missing" if b > a + 2 else f"{a + 1} missing")
                elif b < a:
                    issues.append(f"{b} after {a}")
                seen.add(a)
            segment = []
        segment.append(n)
    return ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(issues)) or None

content.text:
The fixes helped, but the two image problems you targeted are only partly solved. Context carried, review flags and recall improved. E009's scanned quantities are still about as wrong as before, and E023's nameplate is still read as one long line. One metric got slightly worse: qty accuracy. All 88 tests pass and `parsed.json` passes the format check.

**Eval against the p2 run** (10 changes)

| metric | p2 | p3 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| silent losses | 0 | 0 | same |
| hallucinated lines | 1 | 1 | same (E023) |
| lost / phantom requests | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | same |
| classification | 24/24 | 24/24 | same |
| line recall | 207/210 | **209/210** | better (E009 rows 20 and 26 found) |
| line precision | 207/208 | **209/210** | better |
| qty | 196/207 (94.7%) | 197/209 (94.3%) | **slightly worse in percent** |
| uom / source | 100% | 100% | same |
| context carried | 206/207 | **209/209** | better (E005-6 no longer repeats "SCH 40") |
| links | 2/2 | 2/2 | same |
| needs_review precision / recall | 2/3 / 2/2 | **2/2 / 2/2** | better (E002 no longer flagged) |

**What got worse:** qty, and only on the scanned form E009. 4 rows that were right are now wrong and 4 wrong ones are now right. The 2 newly found rows came in with the wrong quantity (row 26 says 24 where the key has 48). The total right went up by one, but the percent dropped because more lines were paired. All 12 qty errors are E009. The model reads a quantity from a neighbouring row, so swapped pairs like 12↔16 appear. It still isn't stable on this scan.

**Fixes that didn't work as hoped:**
1. **200 DPI made no difference for gpt-4.1.** E009's input tokens stayed the same (4,159 → 4,127). For high-detail images the API itself shrinks the shortest side to 768px, so a sharper render gets scaled back down before the model sees it. A change that would actually work: split each scanned page into overlapping horizontal strips, giving each row more pixels. That costs more image tokens.
2. **The numbering check didn't fire on E009, and that's correct.** No rows are skipped or repeated now. The misreads are wrong values inside correctly numbered rows, which this check can't see. It still catches dropped or doubled rows.
3. **E023's raw is still the whole nameplate.** The model ignored the "shortest identifying text" rule for this single-item photo, so it still counts as 1 missed line plus 1 made-up line.

| | p2 | p3 |
|---|---|---|
| model calls | 23 | 23 |
| input tokens (served from OpenAI's prompt cache) | 65,813 (36,224) | 71,218 (34,304) |
| output tokens | 18,983 | 18,685 |
| **total** | $0.2292 | **$0.2405** (~$0.0105 per email) |

The ~5% increase comes from the longer prompt, about 230 more tokens per email; image tokens didn't change.

"""Plain data types shared across the pipeline."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any


@dataclass
class Line:
    """One addressable line of text extracted from the email or an attachment."""

    row_id: str  # stable id shown to the model, e.g. "body!B12", "Sheet1!R5", "a.pdf!P1L8"
    text: str
    struck: bool = False  # the whole line is struck through / deleted in the source
    cells: list[str] | None = None  # table cells, when the line is a table row
    style: str | None = None  # e.g. "Heading 2" for a Word heading
    note: str | None = None  # e.g. "struck cells: C5" when only part of a row is struck


@dataclass
class ImagePart:
    """A picture the model should look at (scan page, photo, pasted screenshot)."""

    label: str  # e.g. "IMG_1.jpg" or "scan.pdf page 2"
    png: bytes
    width: int
    height: int


@dataclass
class Doc:
    """What an extractor produced from one source. Extractors never raise; they set `error`."""

    source: str  # "body" or the attachment filename — what goes in line_items[].source
    kind: str  # body | xlsx | csv | docx | pdf | image | html | eml | text | unknown
    lines: list[Line] = field(default_factory=list)
    images: list[ImagePart] = field(default_factory=list)
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # context: sheet names, hidden sheets skipped, ...
    error: str | None = None  # set when the source could not be read at all
    truncated: bool = False  # part of the source was dropped (page cap, size cap)
    skipped: bool = False  # deliberately not used (e.g. logo image) — not an error


@dataclass
class Attachment:
    filename: str
    mime: str
    data: bytes
    inline: bool = False
    content_id: str | None = None


@dataclass
class Email:
    id: str
    headers: dict[str, str | None]
    body: str  # current message text, history removed
    forwarded: str = ""  # forwarded content (counts as the request when one of our reps forwards)
    quoted: str = ""  # quoted reply history (context; source only for revisions / "items 1-3")
    attachments: list[Attachment] = field(default_factory=list)
    sender: str = ""  # bare lower-case address
    internal: bool = False  # sender is one of our own reps
    date: datetime | None = None
    body_kind: str = "text"  # text | html | none — which MIME part the body came from
    image_alts: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # content-id -> HTML alt text


@dataclass
class LineItem:
    raw: str
    description: str
    qty: float | None
    uom: str | None
    source: str


@dataclass
class Result:
    classification: str
    revises: str | None = None
    duplicate_of: str | None = None
    needs_review: bool = False
    review_reason: str | None = None
    line_items: list[LineItem] = field(default_factory=list)

    def to_json(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

def strip_boxes(height: int, strip_h: int = SCAN_STRIP_HEIGHT_PX,
                overlap: int = SCAN_STRIP_OVERLAP_PX) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Top-to-bottom (top, bottom) boxes of overlapping strips covering the full height."""
    if height <= strip_h:
        return [(0, height)]
    step = strip_h - overlap
    tops = list(range(0, height - strip_h, step)) + [height - strip_h]
    return [(t, t + strip_h) for t in dict.fromkeys(tops)]


def _render_scans(name: str, data: bytes, pages: list[int], doc: Doc, mixed: set[int] | None = None) -> None:
    """Pure scans -> a low-detail overview + overlapping high-detail strips (the API would
    shrink a whole page; a strip keeps full width resolution). Text pages with a large
    picture -> one high-detail page image."""
    mixed = mixed or set()
    if len(pages) > MAX_SCAN_PAGES:
        doc.truncated = True
        doc.notes.append(f"{len(pages)} pages need images; only the first {MAX_SCAN_PAGES} were rendered")
        pages = pages[:MAX_SCAN_PAGES]
    doc.notes.append(f"page(s) {pages} sent as images")
    pdf = pdfium.PdfDocument(data)
    try:
        for p in pages:
            pil = pdf[p - 1].render(scale=SCAN_DPI / 72).to_pil()
            boxes = strip_boxes(pil.height)
            if p in mixed or len(boxes) == 1:
                png, w, h = to_png(pil)
                doc.images.append(ImagePart(label=f"{name} page {p}", png=png, width=w, height=h))
                continue
            png, w, h = to_png(pil)
            doc.images.append(ImagePart(label=f"{name} page {p} overview", png=png, width=w, height=h, detail="low"))
            for i, (top, bottom) in enumerate(boxes, start=1):
                png, w, h = to_png(pil.crop((0, top, pil.width, bottom)))
                doc.images.append(ImagePart(label=f"{name} page {p} strip {i} of {len(boxes)}",
                                            png=png, width=w, height=h))
            doc.notes.append(f"page {p}: scanned; sent as a low-detail overview + {len(boxes)} "
                             f"overlapping high-detail strips (top to bottom)")
    finally:
        pdf.close()

Encrypted PDFs we cannot open come back as an error (needs review), never a crash.

from __future__ import annotations

from io import BytesIO

import pdfplumber
import pypdfium2 as pdfium

from rfq.config import MAX_PDF_PAGES, MAX_SCAN_PAGES, SCAN_DPI
from rfq.extractors.image import to_png
from rfq.models import Doc, ImagePart, Line

MIN_TEXT_CHARS = 20  # fewer chars than this on a page = treat it as a scan
LARGE_PICTURE_FRACTION = 0.20  # a picture covering this much of a text page is rendered too


def _h_segments(page) -> list[tuple[float, float, float]]:
    """Horizontal strokes on the page as (x0, x1, y_middle) in top-down coordinates."""
    segs = []
    for ln in page.lines:
        if abs(ln["top"] - ln["bottom"]) < 1.5:
            segs.append((min(ln["x0"], ln["x1"]), max(ln["x0"], ln["x1"]), (ln["top"] + ln["bottom"]) / 2))
    for r in page.rects:
        if r["height"] < 2.0 and r["width"] > 5:
            segs.append((r["x0"], r["x1"], (r["top"] + r["bottom"]) / 2))
    return segs


def _struck(line: dict, segs) -> bool:
    top, bottom, x0, x1 = line["top"], line["bottom"], line["x0"], line["x1"]
    h = bottom - top
    width = max(x1 - x0, 1.0)
    for sx0, sx1, sy in segs:
        if top + 0.3 * h <= sy <= bottom - 0.3 * h:
            overlap = min(x1, sx1) - max(x0, sx0)
            if overlap >= 0.6 * width:
                return True
    return False

def _h_segments(page) -> list[tuple[float, float, float]]:
    """Horizontal strokes on the page as (x0, x1, y_middle) in top-down coordinates."""
    segs = []
    for ln in page.lines:
        if abs(ln["top"] - ln["bottom"]) < 1.5:
            segs.append((min(ln["x0"], ln["x1"]), max(ln["x0"], ln["x1"]), (ln["top"] + ln["bottom"]) / 2))

def _struck(line: dict, segs) -> bool:
    top, bottom, x0, x1 = line["top"], line["bottom"], line["x0"], line["x1"]
    h = bottom - top
    width = max(x1 - x0, 1.0)
    for sx0, sx1, sy in segs:
        if top + 0.3 * h <= sy <= bottom - 0.3 * h:
            overlap = min(x1, sx1) - max(x0, sx0)
            if overlap >= 0.6 * width:
                return True
    return False

    text+picture pages)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path

try:  # .env is optional; a missing python-dotenv must not break the run
    from dotenv import load_dotenv

    load_dotenv(override=False)
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
    pass

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CACHE_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("RFQ_CACHE_DIR") or ROOT / "cache")
RUNS_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("RFQ_RUNS_DIR") or ROOT / "runs")
REPORTS_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("RFQ_REPORTS_DIR") or ROOT / "reports")

MODEL = os.environ.get("RFQ_MODEL", "gpt-4.1")
PROMPT_VERSION = "p4"  # bump on any prompt/schema change -> new cache keys
TEMPERATURE = 0.0
REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S = 120
MAX_RETRIES = 3  # transient errors only (429, 5xx, timeout, connection)
# Runaway protection. Largest dev email has ~50 items; at ~90 output tokens per item (JSON keys +
# a self-contained description) that is ~4.5k tokens + ~300 for reasoning. Cap the list at 100
# items (2x the largest dev list) and the output at 100 * 90 + 1000 = 10k tokens. A runaway
# now costs at most ~$0.08 instead of ~$0.13; a list at the cap is flagged for review.
MAX_LINE_ITEMS = 100
MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 10_000
IMAGE_DETAIL = "high"  # scans and photos of lists need full resolution
MAX_PROMPT_CHARS = 200_000  # rendered text budget per email (~50k tokens); beyond -> truncated + review

# USD per 1M tokens: (input, cached input, output). Check https://openai.com/api/pricing before
# trusting dollar figures; these are the list prices this code was written against.
PRICES = {
    "gpt-4.1": (2.00, 0.50, 8.00),
    "gpt-4.1-mini": (0.40, 0.10, 1.60),
    "gpt-4o": (2.50, 1.25, 10.00),
    "gpt-4o-mini": (0.15, 0.075, 0.60),
}

# Input caps (protect cost and latency on pathological attachments)
MAX_PDF_PAGES = 20  # text pages read per PDF
MAX_SCAN_PAGES = 6  # scanned pages rendered to images per PDF
MAX_IMAGES_PER_EMAIL = 12
MAX_IMAGE_SIDE_PX = 2048  # the API's own high-detail limit; we never send less than it would use
SCAN_DPI = 200
# Scanned pages (no text layer) go as a low-detail overview + overlapping high-detail strips.
# The API shrinks a high-detail image so its SHORT side is <= 768px; a full page therefore loses
# resolution, a wide strip <= 768px tall keeps it. Overlap so no row is cut in every strip.
SCAN_STRIP_HEIGHT_PX = 720
SCAN_STRIP_OVERLAP_PX = 140
MAX_ROWS_PER_SHEET = 2000
MAX_TEXT_LINES = 3000  # per source
MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES = 25 * 1024 * 1024
NESTED_EML_DEPTH = 2
# An inline image this short, or this wide-and-short, is a logo / signature banner
LOGO_MAX_SIDE_PX = 100
LOGO_MIN_ASPECT = 4.0
LOGO_MAX_HEIGHT_PX = 120

VALID_UOMS = ("EA", "FT", "M", "IN", "BX", "PK", "PR", "DZ", "RL", "LB", "SET", "GAL", "BAG", "CS")
CLASSIFICATIONS = (
    "rfq",
    "rfq_revision",
    "purchase_order",
    "vendor_quote",
    "status_inquiry",
    "auto_reply",
    "other",
)
REQUEST_KINDS = ("rfq", "rfq_revision", "purchase_order")
OUR_DOMAIN = "ridgeline-supply.example"


def api_key_present() -> bool:
    """True if a key is configured. Never returns or prints the key itself."""
    return bool(os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", "").strip())

"""Offline cost estimate: render every prompt, count tokens approximately, price them.

Text: ~3.5 characters per token (tables of numbers tokenize worse than prose).
Images: OpenAI's published sizing rules — tile-based (gpt-4o / gpt-4.1 family) or
patch-based (gpt-4.1-mini). Output: ~70 tokens per likely item line + fixed overhead.
These are estimates; the real run logs actual usage.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

from rfq.config import PRICES
from rfq.models import Doc

CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3.5
OUT_TOKENS_PER_ITEM = 70
OUT_OVERHEAD = 120
ITEMS_PER_IMAGE_GUESS = 15


def image_tokens(model: str, w: int, h: int, detail: str = "high") -> int:
    if model.startswith("gpt-4.1-mini") or model.startswith("gpt-4.1-nano"):
        mult = 1.62 if "mini" in model else 2.46
        patches = math.ceil(w / 32) * math.ceil(h / 32)
        if patches > 1536:
            r = math.sqrt(32 * 32 * 1536 / (w * h))
            patches = min(1536, math.ceil(w * r / 32) * math.ceil(h * r / 32))
        return math.ceil(patches * mult)
    base, per_tile = (2833, 5667) if model.startswith("gpt-4o-mini") else (85, 170)
    if detail == "low":
        return base
    s = min(1.0, 2048 / max(w, h))
    w, h = w * s, h * s
    s = min(1.0, 768 / min(w, h))
    w, h = w * s, h * s
    return base + per_tile * math.ceil(w / 512) * math.ceil(h / 512)


@dataclass
class Estimate:
    email: str
    input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    images: int
    cost_usd: float


def estimate_email(email_id: str, model: str, messages: list[dict], docs: list[Doc]) -> Estimate:
    chars = 0
    for m in messages:
        c = m["content"]
        parts = [{"type": "text", "text": c}] if isinstance(c, str) else c
        chars += sum(len(p["text"]) for p in parts if p["type"] == "text")
    imgs = [im for d in docs for im in d.images]
    in_tok = int(chars / CHARS_PER_TOKEN) + sum(image_tokens(model, im.width, im.height) for im in imgs)
    item_like = sum(
        1 for d in docs for ln in d.lines
        if re.search(r"\d", ln.text) and not ln.struck and not ln.row_id.startswith("body!Q")
    )
    out_tok = OUT_OVERHEAD + OUT_TOKENS_PER_ITEM * (item_like + ITEMS_PER_IMAGE_GUESS * len(imgs))
    p_in, _, p_out = PRICES.get(model, (0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    return Estimate(email_id, in_tok, out_tok, len(imgs), (in_tok * p_in + out_tok * p_out) / 1e6)

No rows were duplicated across the overlapping strips: 32 lines, all from the scan, numbered in order.

**What changed:**
- Only pages with no text layer are cut into strips: 720px tall, overlapping by 140px, at full width. Each page also gets one cheap low-detail overview.
- Photos, pasted images, and text pages with a big picture are sent as before.
- The prompt says strips run top to bottom and that a row near a strip edge must be listed once.
- The image cap per email went from 12 to 30, because a scanned page now uses about 5 images.
- All 90 tests pass.

**Caveats:**
- **This is one sample.** It's temperature 0 and came out at exactly 32/32, but it's a single run on a single scan.
- **Cost on a bigger scan:** about $0.013 per scanned page on top of today's cost. A 6-page scan would add about $0.08.

"""One structured-output call per email, behind the cache.

Order: cache hit -> done (no network). Miss + no key / offline -> error outcome (flagged
upstream, never a crash). Miss + key -> call with retries on transient errors only
(429, 5xx, timeout, connection), validate against the schema, one repair turn if invalid,
cache only a valid result.

The API key is read by the OpenAI client from the environment. It is never logged or stored.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from pydantic import ValidationError
from tenacity import Retrying, retry_if_exception, stop_after_attempt, wait_exponential

from rfq.cache import Cache, cache_key
from rfq.config import (MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, MAX_RETRIES, MODEL, PRICES, PROMPT_VERSION,
                        REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S, TEMPERATURE, api_key_present)
from rfq.models import Doc, Email
from rfq.prompt import build_messages, messages_fingerprint
from rfq.schema import Extraction, response_format


@dataclass
class Usage:
    input_tokens: int = 0
    cached_input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0

    def add(self, other: "Usage") -> None:
        self.input_tokens += other.input_tokens
        self.cached_input_tokens += other.cached_input_tokens
        self.output_tokens += other.output_tokens


def cost_usd(model: str, u: Usage) -> float:
    p_in, p_cached, p_out = PRICES.get(model, (0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    fresh = max(0, u.input_tokens - u.cached_input_tokens)
    return (fresh * p_in + u.cached_input_tokens * p_cached + u.output_tokens * p_out) / 1e6


@dataclass
class Outcome:
    extraction: Extraction | None
    key: str
    cache_hit: bool = False
    live_calls: int = 0  # HTTP requests actually sent this run
    usage: Usage = field(default_factory=Usage)  # tokens of the call that produced the answer
    cost_usd: float = 0.0  # what producing the answer cost (also reported for cache hits)
    live_cost_usd: float = 0.0  # what THIS run paid (0 on a cache hit)
    latency_s: float = 0.0
    error: str | None = None
    retryable: bool = False
    prompt_truncated: bool = False
    # every raw response / exception this run, for diagnosis (saved to runs/ when rejected)
    raw_responses: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)


def _transient(e: BaseException) -> bool:
    import openai

    if isinstance(e, (openai.RateLimitError, openai.APITimeoutError, openai.APIConnectionError,
                      openai.InternalServerError)):
        return True
    return isinstance(e, openai.APIStatusError) and getattr(e, "status_code", 0) >= 500


def _usage(resp) -> Usage:
    u = getattr(resp, "usage", None)
    if u is None:
        return Usage()
    details = getattr(u, "prompt_tokens_details", None)
    return Usage(
        input_tokens=int(getattr(u, "prompt_tokens", 0) or 0),
        cached_input_tokens=int(getattr(details, "cached_tokens", 0) or 0) if details else 0,
        output_tokens=int(getattr(u, "completion_tokens", 0) or 0),
    )


def offline() -> bool:
    return os.environ.get("RFQ_OFFLINE", "").strip() not in ("", "0", "false")


class Extractor:
    def __init__(self, model: str = MODEL, cache: Cache | None = None, client=None,
                 wait_max_s: float = 20.0) -> None:
        self.model = model
        self.cache = cache or Cache()
        self._client = client
        self._schema = response_format()
        self._wait_max = wait_max_s

    def _get_client(self):
        if self._client is not None:
            return self._client
        if offline() or not api_key_present():
            return None
        from openai import OpenAI

        self._client = OpenAI(timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S, max_retries=0)  # we retry ourselves
        return self._client

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ public
    def run(self, email: Email, docs: list[Doc], problems: list[str] | None = None) -> Outcome:
        messages, truncated = build_messages(email, docs, problems)
        key = cache_key(self.model, PROMPT_VERSION, self._schema, messages_fingerprint(messages))
        out = Outcome(extraction=None, key=key, prompt_truncated=truncated)

        hit = self.cache.get(key)
        if hit is not None:
            try:
                out.extraction = Extraction.model_validate(hit["response"])
                out.cache_hit = True
                out.usage = Usage(**hit.get("usage", {}))
                out.cost_usd = float(hit.get("cost_usd", 0.0))
                return out
            except (ValidationError, KeyError, TypeError):
                pass  # stale/corrupt entry: treat as a miss

        client = self._get_client()
        if client is None:
            out.error = "model unavailable (no API key or offline) and no cached response"
            out.retryable = True
            return out

        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            self._call_and_validate(client, messages, out)
        except Exception as e:  # anything unexpected: flagged, never a crash
            out.error = f"model call failed: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:300]}"
            out.retryable = _transient(e) or _auth_or_quota(e)
        out.latency_s = round(time.monotonic() - t0, 2)
        out.cost_usd = out.live_cost_usd = round(cost_usd(self.model, out.usage), 6)

        if out.extraction is not None:
            self.cache.put(key, {
                "key": key,
                "email_id": email.id,
                "model": self.model,
                "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
                "created": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
                "usage": out.usage.__dict__,
                "cost_usd": out.cost_usd,
                "response": out.extraction.model_dump(mode="json"),
            })
        return out

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ internals
    def _send(self, client, messages: list[dict], out: Outcome):
        retrying = Retrying(
            retry=retry_if_exception(_transient),
            stop=stop_after_attempt(MAX_RETRIES + 1),
            wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=1, max=self._wait_max),
            reraise=True,
        )
        for attempt in retrying:
            with attempt:
                out.live_calls += 1
                try:
                    resp = client.chat.completions.create(
                        model=self.model,
                        messages=messages,
                        response_format=self._schema,
                        temperature=TEMPERATURE,
                        max_completion_tokens=MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS,
                    )
                except Exception as e:
                    out.raw_responses.append({"call": out.live_calls, "exception": f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:500]}"})
                    raise
                u = _usage(resp)
                out.usage.add(u)
                choice = resp.choices[0]
                out.raw_responses.append({
                    "call": out.live_calls,
                    "finish_reason": choice.finish_reason,
                    "refusal": getattr(choice.message, "refusal", None),
                    "usage": u.__dict__,
                    "content": choice.message.content,
                })
                return resp
        raise RuntimeError("unreachable")

    def _call_and_validate(self, client, messages: list[dict], out: Outcome) -> None:
        resp = self._send(client, messages, out)
        problem, extraction, content = _check(resp)
        if extraction is None and problem and problem.startswith("invalid"):
            repair = messages + [
                {"role": "assistant", "content": content or ""},
                {"role": "user", "content": f"That output was {problem}. Return the corrected JSON only."},
            ]
            resp = self._send(client, repair, out)
            problem, extraction, _ = _check(resp)
        out.extraction = extraction
        if extraction is None:
            out.error = f"model output rejected: {problem}"
            out.retryable = False
        for r in out.raw_responses:
            r.setdefault("verdict", None)
        if out.raw_responses:
            out.raw_responses[-1]["verdict"] = "accepted" if extraction is not None else problem


def _auth_or_quota(e: BaseException) -> bool:
    import openai

    return isinstance(e, (openai.AuthenticationError, openai.PermissionDeniedError))


def _check(resp) -> tuple[str | None, Extraction | None, str | None]:
    """(problem, extraction, raw content). problem starts with 'invalid' when a repair may help."""
    choice = resp.choices[0]
    msg = choice.message
    if getattr(msg, "refusal", None):
        return f"refused: {msg.refusal}", None, None
    if choice.finish_reason == "length":
        return "too long (hit the output token limit)", None, msg.content
    content = msg.content or ""
    try:
        return None, Extraction.model_validate(json.loads(content)), content
    except (ValueError, ValidationError) as e:
        return f"invalid: {str(e)[:400]}", None, content

                        REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S, TEMPERATURE, api_key_present)
from rfq.models import Doc, Email
from rfq.prompt import build_messages, messages_fingerprint
from rfq.schema import Extraction, response_format


@dataclass
class Usage:
    input_tokens: int = 0
    cached_input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0

    def add(self, other: "Usage") -> None:
        self.input_tokens += other.input_tokens
        self.cached_input_tokens += other.cached_input_tokens
        self.output_tokens += other.output_tokens


def cost_usd(model: str, u: Usage) -> float:
    p_in, p_cached, p_out = PRICES.get(model, (0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    fresh = max(0, u.input_tokens - u.cached_input_tokens)
    return (fresh * p_in + u.cached_input_tokens * p_cached + u.output_tokens * p_out) / 1e6


@dataclass
class Outcome:
    extraction: Extraction | None
    key: str
    cache_hit: bool = False
    live_calls: int = 0  # HTTP requests actually sent this run
    usage: Usage = field(default_factory=Usage)  # tokens of the call that produced the answer
    cost_usd: float = 0.0  # what producing the answer cost (also reported for cache hits)
    live_cost_usd: float = 0.0  # what THIS run paid (0 on a cache hit)
    latency_s: float = 0.0
    error: str | None = None
    retryable: bool = False
    prompt_truncated: bool = False
    # every raw response / exception this run, for diagnosis (saved to runs/ when rejected)
    raw_responses: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)


def _transient(e: BaseException) -> bool:
    import openai

    if isinstance(e, (openai.RateLimitError, openai.APITimeoutError, openai.APIConnectionError,
                      openai.InternalServerError)):
        return True
    return isinstance(e, openai.APIStatusError) and getattr(e, "status_code", 0) >= 500


def _usage(resp) -> Usage:
    u = getattr(resp, "usage", None)
    if u is None:
        return Usage()
    details = getattr(u, "prompt_tokens_details", None)
    return Usage(
        input_tokens=int(getattr(u, "prompt_tokens", 0) or 0),
        cached_input_tokens=int(getattr(details, "cached_tokens", 0) or 0) if details else 0,
        output_tokens=int(getattr(u, "completion_tokens", 0) or 0),
    )


def offline() -> bool:
    return os.environ.get("RFQ_OFFLINE", "").strip() not in ("", "0", "false")


class Extractor:
    def __init__(self, model: str = MODEL, cache: Cache | None = None, client=None,
                 wait_max_s: float = 20.0, live_ids: set[str] | None = None) -> None:
        self.model = model
        self.cache = cache or Cache()
        self._client = client
        self._schema = response_format()
        self._wait_max = wait_max_s
        # None = any email may call the model. A set = only these may (parse --retry-failed);
        # every other email is answered from the cache only.
        self.live_ids = live_ids

    def _get_client(self):
        if self._client is not None:
            return self._client
        if offline() or not api_key_present():
            return None
        from openai import OpenAI

        self._client = OpenAI(timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S, max_retries=0)  # we retry ourselves
        return self._client

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ public
    def run(self, email: Email, docs: list[Doc], problems: list[str] | None = None) -> Outcome:
        messages, truncated = build_messages(email, docs, problems)
        key = cache_key(self.model, PROMPT_VERSION, self._schema, messages_fingerprint(messages))
        out = Outcome(extraction=None, key=key, prompt_truncated=truncated)

        hit = self.cache.get(key)
        if hit is not None:
            try:
                out.extraction = Extraction.model_validate(hit["response"])
                out.cache_hit = True
                out.usage = Usage(**hit.get("usage", {}))
                out.cost_usd = float(hit.get("cost_usd", 0.0))
                return out
            except (ValidationError, KeyError, TypeError):
                pass  # stale/corrupt entry: treat as a miss

        client = self._get_client()
        if client is None:
            out.error = "model unavailable (no API key or offline) and no cached response"
            out.retryable = True
            return out

        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            self._call_and_validate(client, messages, out)
        except Exception as e:  # anything unexpected: flagged, never a crash
            out.error = f"model call failed: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:300]}"
            out.retryable = _transient(e) or _auth_or_quota(e)
        out.latency_s = round(time.monotonic() - t0, 2)
        out.cost_usd = out.live_cost_usd = round(cost_usd(self.model, out.usage), 6)

        if out.extraction is not None:
            self.cache.put(key, {
                "key": key,
                "email_id": email.id,
                "model": self.model,
                "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
                "created": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
                "usage": out.usage.__dict__,
                "cost_usd": out.cost_usd,
                "response": out.extraction.model_dump(mode="json"),
            })
        return out

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ internals
    def _send(self, client, messages: list[dict], out: Outcome):
        retrying = Retrying(
            retry=retry_if_exception(_transient),
            stop=stop_after_attempt(MAX_RETRIES + 1),
            wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=min(1.0, self._wait_max), max=self._wait_max),
            reraise=True,
        )
        for attempt in retrying:
            with attempt:
                out.live_calls += 1
                try:
                    resp = client.chat.completions.create(
                        model=self.model,
                        messages=messages,
                        response_format=self._schema,
                        temperature=TEMPERATURE,
                        max_completion_tokens=MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS,
                    )
                except Exception as e:
                    out.raw_responses.append({"call": out.live_calls, "exception": f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:500]}"})
                    raise
                u = _usage(resp)
                out.usage.add(u)
                choice = resp.choices[0]
                out.raw_responses.append({
                    "call": out.live_calls,
                    "finish_reason": choice.finish_reason,
                    "refusal": getattr(choice.message, "refusal", None),
                    "usage": u.__dict__,
                    "content": choice.message.content,
                })
                return resp
        raise RuntimeError("unreachable")

    def _call_and_validate(self, client, messages: list[dict], out: Outcome) -> None:
        resp = self._send(client, messages, out)
        problem, extraction, content = _check(resp)
        if extraction is None and problem and problem.startswith("invalid"):
            repair = messages + [
                {"role": "assistant", "content": content or ""},
                {"role": "user", "content": f"That output was {problem}. Return the corrected JSON only."},
            ]
            resp = self._send(client, repair, out)
            problem, extraction, _ = _check(resp)
        out.extraction = extraction
        if extraction is None:
            out.error = f"model output rejected: {problem}"
            out.retryable = False
        for r in out.raw_responses:
            r.setdefault("verdict", None)
        if out.raw_responses:
            out.raw_responses[-1]["verdict"] = "accepted" if extraction is not None else problem


def _auth_or_quota(e: BaseException) -> bool:
    import openai

    return isinstance(e, (openai.AuthenticationError, openai.PermissionDeniedError))


def _check(resp) -> tuple[str | None, Extraction | None, str | None]:
    """(problem, extraction, raw content). problem starts with 'invalid' when a repair may help."""
    choice = resp.choices[0]
    msg = choice.message
    if getattr(msg, "refusal", None):
        return f"refused: {msg.refusal}", None, None
    if choice.finish_reason == "length":
        return "too long (hit the output token limit)", None, msg.content
    content = msg.content or ""
    try:
        return None, Extraction.model_validate(json.loads(content)), content
    except (ValueError, ValidationError) as e:
        return f"invalid: {str(e)[:400]}", None, content

def resolve_run_dir(run: str | Path) -> Path:
    """A run id under runs/ ("20261115T...", "latest") or a path to a run folder."""
    p = Path(run)
    if (p / "calls.jsonl").exists():
        return p
    q = RUNS_DIR / str(run)
    if (q / "calls.jsonl").exists():
        return q
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"no run log found at {p} or {q}")


def load_failures(run_dir: Path) -> tuple[set[str], set[str]]:
    """(retryable, not retryable) email ids from a run's failures.jsonl."""
    retryable: set[str] = set()
    final: set[str] = set()
    f = run_dir / "failures.jsonl"
    if f.exists():
        for line in f.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if line.strip():
                row = json.loads(line)
                (retryable if row.get("retryable") else final).add(row["email"])
    return retryable, final - retryable


def run_inbox(emails_dir: Path, model: str = MODEL, retry_failed: Path | None = None,
              extractor: Extractor | None = None, runlog: RunLog | None = None
              ) -> tuple[dict[str, dict], RunLog]:
    """CLI entry: process with a run log and write the cost report.

    retry_failed: a previous run folder. Only its retryable failures may call the model; every
    other email is answered from the cache (its earlier successful answer), so the output is the
    complete inbox again, with the failures recovered where the provider now answers.
    """
    extractor = extractor or Extractor(model=model)
    if retry_failed is not None:
        retryable, final = load_failures(retry_failed)
        extractor.live_ids = retryable
        log.warning("retrying %d retryable failure(s) from %s; %d non-retryable left as they were",
                    len(retryable), retry_failed.name, len(final))
    runlog = runlog or RunLog(model=model)
    out = process_inbox(emails_dir, Context(extractor=extractor, runlog=runlog))
    runlog.finish()
    return out, runlog

"""Command line: `rfq parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json` (or `python -m rfq parse ...`)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from rfq.config import MODEL


def _write_json_atomic(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    tmp.replace(path)


def cmd_parse(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    import os

    from rfq.pipeline import run_inbox

    emails_dir = Path(args.emails)
    if not emails_dir.is_dir():
        print(f"--emails: not a directory: {emails_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if args.offline:
        os.environ["RFQ_OFFLINE"] = "1"
    results, runlog = run_inbox(emails_dir, model=args.model)
    _write_json_atomic(Path(args.out), results)
    rows = runlog.rows
    calls = sum(r.get("live_calls", 0) for r in rows)
    hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("cache_hit"))
    errs = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("error"))
    paid = sum(r.get("live_cost_usd", 0) for r in rows)
    print(f"wrote {len(results)} emails to {args.out} | model calls: {calls}, cache hits: {hits}, "
          f"no answer: {errs}, paid this run: ${paid:.4f} | log: {runlog.dir}")
    return 0


def cmd_estimate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Price a run before making it: render every prompt, count tokens approximately."""
    from rfq.estimate import estimate_email
    from rfq.extractors import extract_all, read_problems
    from rfq.mime import parse_message
    from rfq.pipeline import link_inbox
    from rfq.prompt import build_messages

    emails = [parse_message(p.read_bytes(), p.stem) for p in sorted(Path(args.emails).glob("*.eml"))]
    dups, _ = link_inbox(emails)

def resolve_run_dir(run: str | Path) -> Path:
    """A run id under runs/ ("20261115T...", "latest") or a path to a run folder."""
    p = Path(run)
    if (p / "calls.jsonl").exists():
        return p
    q = RUNS_DIR / str(run)
    if (q / "calls.jsonl").exists():
        return q
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"no run log found at {p} or {q}")


def load_failures(run_dir: Path) -> tuple[set[str], set[str]]:
    """(retryable, not retryable) email ids from a run's failures.jsonl."""
    retryable: set[str] = set()
    final: set[str] = set()
    f = run_dir / "failures.jsonl"
    if f.exists():
        for line in f.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if line.strip():
                row = json.loads(line)
                (retryable if row.get("retryable") else final).add(row["email"])
    return retryable, final - retryable


def run_inbox(emails_dir: Path, model: str = MODEL, retry_failed: Path | None = None,
              extractor: Extractor | None = None, runlog: RunLog | None = None
              ) -> tuple[dict[str, dict], RunLog]:
    """CLI entry: process with a run log and write the cost report.

    retry_failed: a previous run folder. Only its retryable failures may call the model; every
    other email is answered from the cache (its earlier successful answer), so the output is the
    complete inbox again, with the failures recovered where the provider now answers.
    """
    extractor = extractor or Extractor(model=model)
    if retry_failed is not None:
        retryable, final = load_failures(retry_failed)
        extractor.live_ids = retryable
        log.warning("retrying %d retryable failure(s) from %s; %d non-retryable left as they were",
                    len(retryable), retry_failed.name, len(final))
    runlog = runlog or RunLog(model=model)
    out = process_inbox(emails_dir, Context(extractor=extractor, runlog=runlog))
    runlog.finish()
    return out, runlog

"""Model-call tests with a fake OpenAI client (no network, no key)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import openai
import pytest

from rfq.cache import Cache
from rfq.llm import Extractor
from rfq.models import Doc, Email, ImagePart, Line
from rfq.prompt import build_messages
from rfq.schema import response_format

GOOD = {"reasoning": "A customer asks us to price one item.", "classification": "rfq",
        "needs_review": False, "review_reason": None, "sheet_decisions": [], "line_items": [
            {"row_id": "body!B1", "image": None, "raw": "4 ea 2in tee", "description": "2in tee", "qty": 4, "uom": "EA"}]}


def _resp(content: str, finish: str = "stop", refusal=None, tokens=(1000, 200)):
    msg = SimpleNamespace(content=content, refusal=refusal)
    usage = SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=tokens[0], completion_tokens=tokens[1],
                            prompt_tokens_details=SimpleNamespace(cached_tokens=0))
    return SimpleNamespace(choices=[SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason=finish)], usage=usage)


class FakeClient:
    """Replays a script of responses / exceptions; records every request."""

    def __init__(self, script):
        self.script = list(script)
        self.requests: list[dict] = []
        self.chat = SimpleNamespace(completions=SimpleNamespace(create=self._create))

    def _create(self, **kw):
        self.requests.append(kw)
        item = self.script.pop(0)
        if isinstance(item, Exception):
            raise item
        return item


def _email() -> tuple[Email, list[Doc]]:
    e = Email(id="T1", headers={"subject": "RFQ"}, body="4 ea 2in tee")
    return e, [Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[Line("body!B1", "4 ea 2in tee")])]


def _transient() -> Exception:
    req = openai._base_client.httpx.Request("POST", "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions") \
        if hasattr(openai._base_client, "httpx") else None
    return openai.APITimeoutError(request=req)


def _ex(tmp_path: Path, script) -> tuple[Extractor, FakeClient]:
    client = FakeClient(script)
    return Extractor(model="gpt-4.1", cache=Cache(tmp_path / "cache"), client=client, wait_max_s=0.01), client


def test_valid_answer_is_cached_and_second_run_makes_no_call(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, client = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    e, docs = _email()
    first = ex.run(e, docs)
    assert first.extraction and not first.cache_hit and first.live_calls == 1
    assert first.cost_usd == pytest.approx((1000 * 2.0 + 200 * 8.0) / 1e6)
    second = ex.run(e, docs)  # script is empty now: any call would raise IndexError
    assert second.cache_hit and second.live_calls == 0 and second.live_cost_usd == 0
    assert second.cost_usd == first.cost_usd  # cost to produce is still reported
    assert len(client.requests) == 1


def test_request_uses_strict_schema_and_temperature_zero(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, client = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    ex.run(*_email())
    req = client.requests[0]
    assert req["response_format"] == response_format() and req["temperature"] == 0
    assert req["messages"][0]["role"] == "system"


def test_invalid_then_repaired(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, client = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp('{"classification": "rfq"}'), _resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction and out.live_calls == 2
    assert "corrected JSON" in client.requests[1]["messages"][-1]["content"]


def test_invalid_twice_is_error_and_not_cached(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp("not json"), _resp("still not json")])
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction is None and "rejected" in out.error and not out.retryable
    assert not list((tmp_path / "cache").glob("*.json")) if (tmp_path / "cache").exists() else True


def test_transient_errors_are_retried(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_transient(), _transient(), _resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction and out.live_calls == 3


def test_transient_errors_exhausted_is_retryable_failure(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_transient()] * 4)
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction is None and out.retryable and out.live_calls == 4


def test_refusal_and_length_are_errors(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp("", refusal="no")])
    assert "refused" in ex.run(*_email()).error
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp('{"result":', finish="length")])
    assert "too long" in ex.run(*_email()).error


def test_no_key_and_cache_miss_is_flagged_not_crash(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex = Extractor(model="gpt-4.1", cache=Cache(tmp_path / "cache"))  # offline via conftest
    out = ex.run(*_email())
    assert out.extraction is None and out.retryable and "no cached response" in out.error


def test_cache_key_changes_with_content_model_and_prompt_version(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp(json.dumps(GOOD))] * 3)
    e, docs = _email()
    k1 = ex.run(e, docs).key
    docs2 = [Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[Line("body!B1", "5 ea 2in tee")])]
    assert ex.run(e, docs2).key != k1
    import rfq.llm as llm

    monkeypatch.setattr(llm, "PROMPT_VERSION", "p-test")
    assert ex.run(e, docs).key != k1


def test_images_go_as_vision_parts() -> None:
    e = Email(id="T2", headers={}, body="see photo")
    docs = [Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[Line("body!B1", "see photo")]),
            Doc(source="IMG_1.jpg", kind="image", images=[ImagePart("IMG_1.jpg", b"\x89PNG", 10, 10)])]
    messages, _ = build_messages(e, docs)
    parts = messages[1]["content"]
    assert any(p["type"] == "image_url" and p["image_url"]["url"].startswith("data:image/png;base64,") for p in parts)
    assert any(p["type"] == "text" and p["text"] == "IMAGE label: IMG_1.jpg" for p in parts)


def test_schema_field_order_reasoning_first_and_line_cap() -> None:
    from rfq.config import MAX_LINE_ITEMS

    s = response_format()["json_schema"]["schema"]
    assert list(s["properties"]) == ["reasoning", "classification", "needs_review", "review_reason",
                                     "sheet_decisions", "line_items"]
    assert s["properties"]["line_items"]["maxItems"] == MAX_LINE_ITEMS
    assert "oneOf" not in json.dumps(s) and "anyOf" not in json.dumps(s["properties"]["classification"])


def test_read_problems_are_in_the_prompt() -> None:
    e, docs = _email()
    messages, _ = build_messages(e, docs, ["rfq.pdf: PDF is password-protected"])
    text = messages[1]["content"][0]["text"]
    assert "=== READ PROBLEMS ===" in text and "rfq.pdf: PDF is password-protected" in text


def test_rejected_output_saved_to_run_folder(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    from rfq.costlog import RunLog

    ex, _ = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp('{"reasoning": "x"', finish="length")])
    log = RunLog("gpt-4.1", runs_dir=tmp_path / "runs", reports_dir=tmp_path / "reports")
    e, docs = _email()

"""Model-call tests with a fake OpenAI client (no network, no key)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

from rfq.cache import Cache
from rfq.llm import Extractor
from rfq.models import Doc, Email, ImagePart, Line
from rfq.prompt import build_messages
from rfq.schema import response_format

GOOD = {"reasoning": "A customer asks us to price one item.", "classification": "rfq",
        "needs_review": False, "review_reason": None, "sheet_decisions": [], "line_items": [
            {"row_id": "body!B1", "image": None, "raw": "4 ea 2in tee", "description": "2in tee", "qty": 4, "uom": "EA"}]}


def _resp(content: str, finish: str = "stop", refusal=None, tokens=(1000, 200)):
    msg = SimpleNamespace(content=content, refusal=refusal)
    usage = SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=tokens[0], completion_tokens=tokens[1],
                            prompt_tokens_details=SimpleNamespace(cached_tokens=0))
    return SimpleNamespace(choices=[SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason=finish)], usage=usage)


class FakeClient:
    """Replays a script of responses / exceptions; records every request."""

    def __init__(self, script):
        self.script = list(script)
        self.requests: list[dict] = []
        self.chat = SimpleNamespace(completions=SimpleNamespace(create=self._create))

    def _create(self, **kw):
        self.requests.append(kw)
        item = self.script.pop(0)
        if isinstance(item, Exception):
            raise item
        return item


def _email() -> tuple[Email, list[Doc]]:
    e = Email(id="T1", headers={"subject": "RFQ"}, body="4 ea 2in tee")
    return e, [Doc(source="body", kind="body", lines=[Line("body!B1", "4 ea 2in tee")])]


_URL = "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions"


def _transient() -> Exception:
    """A request timeout, as the SDK raises it."""
    return openai.APITimeoutError(request=openai._base_client.httpx2.Request("POST", _URL))


def status_error(code: int) -> Exception:
    """A real SDK status error (500 -> InternalServerError, 429 -> RateLimitError, ...)."""
    httpx2 = openai._base_client.httpx2
    resp = httpx2.Response(code, request=httpx2.Request("POST", _URL), json={"error": {"message": "x"}})
    cls = {500: openai.InternalServerError, 502: openai.InternalServerError, 503: openai.InternalServerError,
           429: openai.RateLimitError, 400: openai.BadRequestError, 401: openai.AuthenticationError}[code]
    return cls(f"HTTP {code}", response=resp, body=None)


def _ex(tmp_path: Path, script) -> tuple[Extractor, FakeClient]:
    client = FakeClient(script)
    return Extractor(model="gpt-4.1", cache=Cache(tmp_path / "cache"), client=client, wait_max_s=0.01), client


def test_valid_answer_is_cached_and_second_run_makes_no_call(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ex, client = _ex(tmp_path, [_resp(json.dumps(GOOD))])
    e, docs = _email()
    first = ex.run(e, docs)
    assert first.extraction and not first.cache_hit and first.live_calls == 1
    assert first.cost_usd == pytest.approx((1000 * 2.0 + 200 * 8.0) / 1e6)
    second = ex.run(e, docs)  # script is empty now: any call would raise IndexError
    assert second.cache_hit and second.live_calls == 0 and second.live_cost_usd == 0
    assert second.cost_usd == first.cost_usd  # cost to produce is still reported
    assert len(client.requests) == 1

"""Whole-inbox resilience: provider down, partial outage, and `parse --retry-failed` recovery.

Uses fake OpenAI clients (no network). Each fake answers per email from the request text.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from email.message import EmailMessage
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

from rfq.cache import Cache
from rfq.cli import main
from rfq.costlog import RunLog
from rfq.llm import Extractor
from rfq.pipeline import load_failures, resolve_run_dir, run_inbox
from tests.test_llm import _resp, status_error


def _inbox(tmp: Path, n: int = 3) -> Path:
    d = tmp / "emails"
    d.mkdir()
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        m = EmailMessage()
        m["From"], m["To"] = f"buyer{i}@cust{i}.example", "rfq@ridgeline-supply.example"
        m["Subject"], m["Date"] = f"RFQ {i}", f"Mon, 0{i} Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0600"
        m["Message-ID"] = f"<m{i}@cust{i}.example>"
        m.set_content(f"Please quote {i + 3} ea 2in tee")
        (d / f"M{i}.eml").write_bytes(m.as_bytes())
    return d


def _answer() -> str:
    return json.dumps({
        "reasoning": "A customer asks us to price a tee.", "classification": "rfq",
        "needs_review": False, "review_reason": None, "sheet_decisions": [],
        "line_items": [{"row_id": "body!B1", "image": None, "raw": "tee", "description": "2in tee",
                        "qty": None, "uom": "EA"}],
    })


class Fake:
    """fail(subject) -> True means that email's call raises a 503."""

    def __init__(self, fail=lambda text: False):
        self.fail = fail
        self.calls: list[str] = []
        self.chat = SimpleNamespace(completions=SimpleNamespace(create=self._create))

    def _create(self, **kw):
        text = kw["messages"][1]["content"][0]["text"]
        self.calls.append(text)
        if self.fail(text):
            raise status_error(503)
        return _resp(_answer())


def _run(tmp: Path, emails: Path, client, retry: Path | None = None):
    ex = Extractor(model="gpt-4.1", cache=Cache(tmp / "cache"), client=client, wait_max_s=0.01)
    log = RunLog("gpt-4.1", runs_dir=tmp / "runs", reports_dir=tmp / "reports")
    return run_inbox(emails, retry_failed=retry, extractor=ex, runlog=log)


def test_provider_down_every_email_flagged_retryable_no_crash(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    emails = _inbox(tmp_path)
    down = Fake(fail=lambda t: True)
    out, log = _run(tmp_path, emails, down)
    assert set(out) == {"M1", "M2", "M3"}
    for r in out.values():
        assert r["needs_review"] and "InternalServerError" in r["review_reason"] and r["line_items"] == []
    retryable, final = load_failures(log.dir)
    assert retryable == {"M1", "M2", "M3"} and not final
    assert len(down.calls) == 3 * 4  # each email: first try + 3 retries, then give up
    assert not list((tmp_path / "cache").glob("*.json")) if (tmp_path / "cache").exists() else True
    assert "emails with no model answer | 3" in (tmp_path / "reports" / "cost.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def test_retry_failed_recovers_after_outage(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    emails = _inbox(tmp_path)
    _, failed_run = _run(tmp_path, emails, Fake(fail=lambda t: True))

Step 8 is now fully covered, and all 100 tests pass. `--retry-failed` didn't exist before, so I built it; the other gaps were missing tests.

**Coverage:**

| case | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| timeout | ✔ retried then success; ✔ exhausted → retryable | unchanged |
| 500 server error | not tested | ✔ retried then success |
| 429 rate limit | not tested | ✔ 3 retries then success; ✔ exhausted → retryable, 4 calls total |
| 400 bad request | not tested | ✔ not retried, not retryable |
| 401 bad key | not tested | ✔ not retried now, marked retryable (fix the key, then retry) |
| provider down, whole inbox | not tested | ✔ every email flagged for review, all retryable, nothing cached, no crash, cost report says 3 with no answer |
| `parse --retry-failed <run>` | **not built** | ✔ built and tested (below) |

**What `--retry-failed` does:**
- It takes a run ID under `runs/`, `latest`, or a path to a run folder.
- It reads that run's `failures.jsonl`. Only the retryable failures may call the model; every other email comes from the cache, so the output is again the complete `parsed.json`.
- Failures marked not retryable (like a rejected answer) aren't paid for again; they stay flagged.
- A run that doesn't exist gives a clear error and exit code 2.

**Recovery tests:**
- **Provider down then back up:** the retry made exactly 3 calls and all 3 emails came back clean. A plain re-run after that made 0 calls with identical output.
- **Partial outage:** only the one failed email was re-called. The others came back unchanged from the cache.
- **Real dev inbox:** `--retry-failed latest` (no failures in that run) made 0 calls and reproduced `parsed.json` exactly. Logs went to the scratchpad, so `reports/` and `runs/latest/` are untouched.

**Fix along the way:** the retry wait had a 1-second minimum that ignored the configured maximum. A test asking for a 0.01 s wait slept a full second per retry. In production the waits are still 1–20 s.

"""Replay the synthetic inbox (tests/synthetic/) offline from its committed cache and check each
email against tests/synthetic/expected.json. No network: conftest forces offline mode.

To refresh after a prompt change (costs ~$0.10):
    set RFQ_CACHE_DIR=tests/synthetic/cache  then  rfq parse --emails tests/synthetic/emails --out <tmp>.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from eval.eval import mentions
from rfq.cache import Cache
from rfq.costlog import RunLog
from rfq.llm import Extractor
from rfq.pipeline import Context, process_inbox

SYN = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "synthetic"
EXPECTED = {k: v for k, v in json.loads((SYN / "expected.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")).items()
            if not k.startswith("_")}


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def replay(tmp_path_factory):
    tmp = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("syn")
    log = RunLog("gpt-4.1", runs_dir=tmp / "runs", reports_dir=tmp / "reports")
    out = process_inbox(SYN / "emails", Context(extractor=Extractor(cache=Cache(SYN / "cache")), runlog=log))
    return out, log


def test_every_synthetic_email_replays_from_cache(replay) -> None:
    out, log = replay
    assert set(out) == set(EXPECTED)
    missing = [r["email"] for r in log.rows if r.get("error")]
    assert not missing, f"no cached answer for {missing}: re-record the synthetic cache"
    assert sum(r.get("live_calls", 0) for r in log.rows) == 0


def check(got: dict, exp: dict) -> list[str]:
    problems = []
    for f in ("classification", "needs_review", "revises"):
        if got[f] != exp[f]:
            problems.append(f"{f}: got {got[f]!r}, expected {exp[f]!r}")
    lines = got["line_items"]
    if "n_lines" in exp and len(lines) != exp["n_lines"]:
        problems.append(f"n_lines: got {len(lines)}, expected {exp['n_lines']}")
    if "qtys" in exp:
        got_q = Counter(None if q is None else float(q) for q in (li["qty"] for li in lines))
        exp_q = Counter(None if q is None else float(q) for q in exp["qtys"])
        if got_q != exp_q:
            problems.append(f"qtys: got {sorted(got_q.elements(), key=str)}, expected {sorted(exp_q.elements(), key=str)}")
    descs = " | ".join(li["description"] for li in lines)
    for m in exp.get("mention", []):
        if not mentions(descs, m):
            problems.append(f"no description mentions {m!r}")
    for m in exp.get("not_mention", []):
        if mentions(descs, m):
            problems.append(f"a description mentions {m!r}")
    if "source" in exp and any(li["source"] != exp["source"] for li in lines):
        problems.append(f"source: got {sorted({li['source'] for li in lines})}, expected {exp['source']!r}")
    return problems


@pytest.mark.parametrize("sid", sorted(EXPECTED))
def test_synthetic_email(replay, sid: str) -> None:
    out, _ = replay
    problems = check(out[sid], EXPECTED[sid])
    assert not problems, f"{sid} ({EXPECTED[sid]['situation']}): " + "; ".join(problems)

content.text:
Nothing fails: all 9 synthetic emails match their expected results, replayed offline from cache with 0 model calls.

**What I added:**
- **`tests/synthetic/build_synthetic.py`:** generates the 9 emails, including a real `.xlsx` with a struck-through row and a `.docx` with an embedded "photo" of a list. All names and parts are invented. The generated `.eml` files are committed, because Office files embed timestamps and rebuilding would change their cache keys.
- **`tests/synthetic/emails/S01–S09.eml`:** one email per situation you listed.
- **`tests/synthetic/expected.json`:** the expected result for each email, written from the README *before* the model run. It covers classification, needs_review, revises, line count, quantities, mention/not-mention, and source.
- **`tests/synthetic/cache/`:** the 9 recorded answers, $0.0433 for one real run.
- **`tests/test_synthetic.py`:** replays offline and fails if any answer is missing from the cache. Each email is a separate test case, so one failure shows by name.

**Results:**

| | situation | result |
|---|---|---|
| S01 | out-of-office auto-reply | ✔ `auto_reply`, no lines |
| S02 | "same as our last order, but double it" | ✔ `rfq`, review: "items only identified by reference to a previous order" |
| S03 | revision, original not in the inbox | ✔ `rfq_revision`, `revises: null`, 4 lines, gate valve qty changed 4 → 6, check valve added |
| S04 | Excel row struck through | ✔ 3 lines, unions excluded |
| S05 | Word file with a photo of a list | ✔ 4 lines read from the picture, source = the `.docx` |
| S06 | remittance advice | ✔ `other` |
| S07 | "we went with another supplier" | ✔ `other` |
| S08 | PO naming only a quote number | ✔ `purchase_order`, needs_review |
| S09 | "twelve", "six", "a couple" | ✔ qty 12, 6, null, and no review flag |

**Weak spots my expected results don't catch** (I haven't tuned anything):
1. **S08 passes only because of the code safety net.** The model returned a PO with no lines and didn't flag it itself. The review reason is the generic guard text ("no line items could be extracted"). A rep would want "PO 77812 refers to quote Q-26-05120; items not in the email."
2. **S09's caps borrow a spec the email didn't give.** "A couple of 2" caps" became "2" caps, schedule 40, butt weld". The "same" in the email applies to the tees, not the caps, so this is probably an invented spec. My expected results only check for "cap", so this passes.
3. **S05's descriptions start with the list title** ("Shop list - boiler room: …"). It's harmless noise, but not useful in a description.
4. **S03's changed line uses the change sentence as `raw`** ("Item 2 - make it 6 instead of 4.") rather than the original line it changes. Neither choice is clearly what a grader would pair against.

All 110 tests pass.

"""Central settings. The API key is read from the environment only and never logged."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path

try:  # .env is optional; a missing python-dotenv must not break the run
    from dotenv import load_dotenv

    load_dotenv(override=False)
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
    pass

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CACHE_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("RFQ_CACHE_DIR") or ROOT / "cache")
RUNS_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("RFQ_RUNS_DIR") or ROOT / "runs")
REPORTS_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("RFQ_REPORTS_DIR") or ROOT / "reports")

MODEL = os.environ.get("RFQ_MODEL", "gpt-4.1")
PROMPT_VERSION = "p4"  # bump on any prompt/schema change -> new cache keys
TEMPERATURE = 0.0
REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S = 120
MAX_RETRIES = 3  # transient errors only (429, 5xx, timeout, connection)
# Runaway protection. Largest dev email has ~50 items; at ~90 output tokens per item (JSON keys +
# a self-contained description) that is ~4.5k tokens + ~300 for reasoning. Cap the list at 100
# items (2x the largest dev list) and the output at 100 * 90 + 1000 = 10k tokens. A runaway
# now costs at most ~$0.08 instead of ~$0.13; a list at the cap is flagged for review.
MAX_LINE_ITEMS = 100
MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 10_000
IMAGE_DETAIL = "high"  # scans and photos of lists need full resolution
MAX_PROMPT_CHARS = 200_000  # rendered text budget per email (~50k tokens); beyond -> truncated + review

# USD per 1M tokens: (input, cached input, output). Check https://openai.com/api/pricing before
# trusting dollar figures; these are the list prices this code was written against.
PRICES = {
    "gpt-4.1": (2.00, 0.50, 8.00),
    "gpt-4.1-mini": (0.40, 0.10, 1.60),
    "gpt-4o": (2.50, 1.25, 10.00),
    "gpt-4o-mini": (0.15, 0.075, 0.60),
}

# Input caps (protect cost and latency on pathological attachments)
MAX_PDF_PAGES = 20  # text pages read per PDF
MAX_SCAN_PAGES = 6  # scanned pages rendered to images per PDF
MAX_IMAGES_PER_EMAIL = 30  # scans use 1 overview + ~3 strips per page
MAX_IMAGE_SIDE_PX = 2048  # the API's own high-detail limit; we never send less than it would use
SCAN_DPI = 200
# Scanned pages (no text layer) go as a low-detail overview + overlapping high-detail strips.
# The API shrinks a high-detail image so its SHORT side is <= 768px; a full page therefore loses
# resolution, a wide strip <= 768px tall keeps it. Overlap so no row is cut in every strip.
SCAN_STRIP_HEIGHT_PX = 720
SCAN_STRIP_OVERLAP_PX = 140
MAX_ROWS_PER_SHEET = 2000
MAX_TEXT_LINES = 3000  # per source
MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES = 25 * 1024 * 1024

# An inline image this short, or this wide-and-short, is a logo / signature banner

LOGO_MIN_ASPECT = 4.0
LOGO_MAX_HEIGHT_PX = 120

"""Replay the synthetic inbox (tests/synthetic/) offline from its committed cache and check each
email against tests/synthetic/expected.json. No network: conftest forces offline mode.

To refresh after a prompt change (costs ~$0.10):
    set RFQ_CACHE_DIR=tests/synthetic/cache  then  rfq parse --emails tests/synthetic/emails --out <tmp>.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from eval.eval import mentions
from rfq.cache import Cache
from rfq.costlog import RunLog
from rfq.llm import Extractor
from rfq.pipeline import Context, process_inbox

SYN = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "synthetic"
EXPECTED = {k: v for k, v in json.loads((SYN / "expected.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")).items()
            if not k.startswith("_")}


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def replay(tmp_path_factory):
    tmp = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("syn")
    log = RunLog("gpt-4.1", runs_dir=tmp / "runs", reports_dir=tmp / "reports")
    out = process_inbox(SYN / "emails", Context(extractor=Extractor(cache=Cache(SYN / "cache")), runlog=log))
    return out, log


def test_every_synthetic_email_replays_from_cache(replay) -> None:
    out, log = replay
    assert set(out) == set(EXPECTED)
    missing = [r["email"] for r in log.rows if r.get("error")]
    assert not missing, f"no cached answer for {missing}: re-record the synthetic cache"
    assert sum(r.get("live_calls", 0) for r in log.rows) == 0


def check(got: dict, exp: dict) -> list[str]:
    problems = []
    for f in ("classification", "needs_review", "revises"):
        if got[f] != exp[f]:
            problems.append(f"{f}: got {got[f]!r}, expected {exp[f]!r}")
    lines = got["line_items"]
    if "n_lines" in exp and len(lines) != exp["n_lines"]:
        problems.append(f"n_lines: got {len(lines)}, expected {exp['n_lines']}")
    if "qtys" in exp:
        got_q = Counter(None if q is None else float(q) for q in (li["qty"] for li in lines))
        exp_q = Counter(None if q is None else float(q) for q in exp["qtys"])
        if got_q != exp_q:
            problems.append(f"qtys: got {sorted(got_q.elements(), key=str)}, expected {sorted(exp_q.elements(), key=str)}")
    descs = " | ".join(li["description"] for li in lines)
    for m in exp.get("mention", []):
        if not mentions(descs, m):
            problems.append(f"no description mentions {m!r}")
    for m in exp.get("not_mention", []):
        if mentions(descs, m):
            problems.append(f"a description mentions {m!r}")
    if "source" in exp and any(li["source"] != exp["source"] for li in lines):
        problems.append(f"source: got {sorted({li['source'] for li in lines})}, expected {exp['source']!r}")
    return problems


@pytest.mark.parametrize("sid", sorted(EXPECTED))
def test_synthetic_email(replay, sid: str) -> None:
    out, _ = replay
    problems = check(out[sid], EXPECTED[sid])
    assert not problems, f"{sid} ({EXPECTED[sid]['situation']}): " + "; ".join(problems)

I made both fixes, but neither came out clean. #1 now works on S08 but wrongly flags two dev emails, and #2 didn't take effect at all. All other dev metrics are unchanged.

**Dev eval against p4** (2 changes)

| metric | p4 | p5 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| silent losses / hallucinated lines | 0 / 1 | 0 / 1 | same |
| lost / phantom requests | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | same |
| classification | 24/24 | 24/24 | same |
| line recall / precision | 209/210 / 209/210 | 209/210 / 209/210 | same |
| qty / uom / source / context carried | 100% each | 100% each | same |
| links | 2/2 | 2/2 | same |
| **needs_review precision** | **2/2** | **2/4** | **worse** |
| needs_review recall | 2/2 | 2/2 | same |

**What got worse:** the new reference rule (#1) now also fires on two dev purchase orders whose items *are* in the email:
- **E015:** "PO refers to a quote from last week… Items are taken from the attached PO only." The PO is attached and lists every item.
- **E020:** "PO refers to quote Q-26-04418; its items are not in this email but are listed in the quoted history." The model's own reason contradicts itself.

The rule as I wrote it fires on any mention of a quote number. It should only fire when the items can't be found anywhere: not in the body, the attachments or the quoted history.

**Synthetic tests** (re-recorded under `p5`, $0.0468): 109 of 110 tests pass, and 1 fails.
- **#1 works on S08:** the model now flags it itself, with the reason "PO refers to quote Q-26-05120; its items are not in this email." S02 also names its reference: "Request refers to 'our last order'…".
- **#2 didn't work. S09 still fails:** the caps line is still "2" caps, schedule 40, butt weld". The new "don't borrow specs across item types" rule changed nothing. I'm leaving that test failing because it shows the real state.

**Cost** (`reports/cost.md`)

| | p4 | p5 |
|---|---|---|
| input tokens (served from OpenAI's prompt cache) | 83,720 (30,464) | 88,320 (29,184) |
| output tokens | 19,190 | 18,586 |
| **cost to produce these answers** | $0.2753 | **$0.2816** (+$0.006, longer prompt) |

**Suggested next steps** (not done):
- **#1:** narrow the rule to "only when the referenced items appear nowhere in the email, its attachments or its quoted history". Citing a quote number alongside a full item list isn't a reason for review.
- **#2:** prompt wording alone didn't move the model. One option is a worked example of the wrong vs. right description. The other is to accept it and record it in `DECISIONS.md` as a known limitation (spec carried onto vaguely related items).

**Cleanup:** the `p4` answers are still in `cache/` and `tests/synthetic/cache/`. Say if you want them removed.
